News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

Sports.title: EFL club’s former stadium set to be largely demolished with historic stands knocked down in fresh plans
Sports.content:
ROTHERHAM UNITED’S former Millmoor home will be largely demolished if plans submitted to local councillors are approved.

The project, if given the green light, is set to see two of the ground’s stands torn down, in addition to some surrounding buildings.



The Millers left Millmoor in 2008 after new owner Tony Stewart failed to agree a deal with former chief Ken Booth.

Booth had saved the club from financial turmoil in 1987 but decided to depart in 2004 amid rising debts following the ITV Digital collapse that crippled much of the EFL.



The Booth family gave the club away to a supporter group for £1, while also writing off its overdraft.

But in the deal they insisted on keeping several assets; the club’s Hooton Lodge training ground, land on which stood the Tivoli nightclub and even priority ticket access among them.



Most significantly, the deal saw the Booth family retain ownership of Millmoor.

A turbulent few years followed, as the club edged closer to oblivion.



When Stewart rescued Rotherham after they’d been plunged into ruin once again, he was unable to secure Millmoor as part of his deal to acquire the Yorkshire club from the Booth family, despite his best efforts.

As a result, the Millers spent four years at the Don Valley athletics stadium in Sheffield before moving into the swanky modern New York Stadium a stone’s throw from Millmoor.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

At the time of Rotherham’s exit they had been halfway through a rebuild of the club’s main stand… a rebuild that would never finish.

For more than a decade after the Millers’ exit, Millmoor was left largely to rot.



Rotherham Titans, a second-tier rugby club, had shared the ground with United on occasion during the early 2000s.

In 2011 they attempted to strike a deal to use Millmoor, three years on from the football club’s departure.

But like Stewart, they could not strike a deal with the Booth family.

The ground began to fall into a state of disrepair, with its stands growing ever more dilapidated.



Remarkably, much of Millmoor did actually stay relatively intact down the years, with its pitch somewhat maintained, its goals still standing and most of its signage remaining.

In a further twist, Millmoor was partially restored in 2024 following a financial injection by Ken Booth Jr, the former Rotherham owner’s son.

Then 78, Booth Jr told the Rotherham Advertiser at the time: “The place was in a sad state. We had kids breaking in, trying to rip seats out, climbing the floodlight pylon, kicking a ball about.

“It was time for something to be done.”



Following restoration work, Millmoor was able to open its doors once again, with matches taking place on the hallowed turf.

Local junior teams were able to play there, relishing the opportunity to compete at a ground that first opened its doors in 1907 and that had housed a 25,170 crowd in its heyday.

In the summer of 2025 it was confirmed that Millmoor would become the new home of former WSL side Doncaster Belles.

This marked the return of regular senior football at the ground for the first time since 2008.



But it wasn’t to last… as in earlier this year the Booth family business went into administration.

CF Booth and its assets, including Millmoor, were subsequently acquired by the Ron Hull Group.

Following news of CF Booth’s demise, Doncaster Belles left Millmoor, moving to the SL2 Rail Stadium in Retford for the remainder of their season.

A statement by the Ron Hull Group, as shared by Rotherham Business News in May, read: “The buildings and structures selected in the current application to demolish are all in a poor condition due to years of neglect and are suffering from a general lack of maintenance, specifically elements like roof finishes and the structures themselves.



“It is assumed this situation accelerated in the period since Rotherham United football Club vacated the site.

“The current main stand is only partially completed, and has been exposed to the elements since at least 2007.

“The high cost of repair, yet alone proceed to complete this stand would be excessive given that there are very limited numbers of possible users of the ground. Thus meaning it is unbuyable.”

Plans submitted to local councillors involve demolishing the Millmoor Lane Stand and Railway Stand – in addition to removing pitch lighting columns and various other buildings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If approved, demolition work is targeted to be completed by January next year.



It then remains to be seen what will become of the site, which meant so much to so many people for the best part of a century up to 2008.

Sports.title: Uefa, Burnham and Lineker blast Fifa plan to flog World Cup to investors as bombshell plot sparks football civil war
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino plans to flog stakes in the World Cup in a shameless scheme that could net him tens of millions.

The plot to sell off the competition to private investors would lead to a company being formed — likely headed by Infantino.



People close to his pal Donald Trump have reportedly been consulted.

The idea sparked a furious reaction from fans and triggered a footie civil war — with European governing body Uefa warning it “crosses a line”.



Senior football figures warned the plan is a potential “nuclear bomb” for the game.

PM Andy Burnham said: “The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport.

“Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans.” Sky News reported that European nations would consider boycotting the World Cup if Fifa president Gianni Infantino pushes ahead with the scheme.

US venture capital firm Thrive is expected to lead the proposed investor group for new subsidiary Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE). Bank JP Morgan is said to be involved.

Thrive Capital’s founder Joshua Kushner, 41, is the brother of Mr Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Each of Fifa’s 211 member associations would be given a stake potentially each worth £15million, which they could retain or sell to raise income for themselves.



They could vote on the plan at March’s Fifa Congress in Morocco. Potential investors would have to sign non-disclosure agreements and Fifa would own a majority stake in the company, reported The Times.

Infantino could become its commissioner, once his presidential term expires in 2031. His salary could hit £48million, the same as NFL commissioner Roger Goodell.

Some non-binding agreements setting out the terms of the arrangement have already been signed, it was reported.



Setting out the idea, Fifa said: “Fifa is always on the lookout for innovative projects that can boost the development of football around the world and is always open to reviewing proposals submitted to it.

“We are starting a consultation process. As the Fifa president stated on July 18 during a meeting with all Fifa member associations, the priority now is to ‘unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that Fifa has’ after the Fifa World Cup 2026 success.

“Fifa makes its decisions democratically, and a proposal that Fifa has received and is currently reviewing will soon be presented to the 211 member associations and the Fifa Council, who will be the sole final decision-makers.”

Fifa said money available to member associations would increase from £6million to £20million for the 2027-30 cycle “and grow steadily thereafter cycle-on-cycle”.

In its strongly-worded response, Uefa said: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. Uefa takes it extremely seriously.



“So should every national football association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the game’s future.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa’s to sell.”

Even ex-Fifa president Sepp Blatter laid into the plan saying: “The close relationship between the Fifa president and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football. No one has the right to sell our game.”



Footie writer Henry Winter said: “Outside investors should be nowhere near the greatest sporting prize.”

Fifa generated billions through TV rights, sponsorship and ticket and hospitality sales from the World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico. Infantino said earlier this month that a South American proposal to expand from 48 to 64 teams would “definitely” be looked at.

But there are fears a bigger World Cup — and Club World Cup — could place more strain on domestic schedules.

Infantino was at the heart of several World Cup scandals including Trump asking him to review a red card for USA striker Folarin Balogun, which was then rescinded.

There was controversy over hydration breaks, VAR calls and alleged bias to Argentina and its superstar striker Lionel Messi.



FIFA’S WORLD CUP SELL-OFF PLAN Fifa would set up a firm for the “operational delivery of Fifa tournaments” called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which will effectively control the men’s and women’s World Cups and Club World Cup Fifa would then own the majority share in the company — but investors could purchase 20 to 30 per cent which could amount to billions of dollars Each of Fifa’s 211 member associations would also be given a stake worth approximately £15m which they could keep or sell Infantino would then be in line to run the company after he steps down as head of Fifa One proposed investor is Joshua Kushner — a younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner

Ex-Liverpool player Stan Collymore suggested Uefa should split from Fifa, adding: “Uefa’s power base is 10, 20, 1,000 times more. It’s where all the players, storied clubs, monster crowds, greatest coaches, referees and sheer size of football infrastructure is.”

Gary Lineker reposted the BBC’s Instagram story with the comment “Nothing surprises me any more” and a vomit emoji.

Sports broadcaster Richard Keys said: “The WC is not this fool’s to sell. Enough….”

Meanwhile, insiders said England’s FA was “completely unaware” of Fifa’s plans until its statement yesterday.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fifa played down claims Infantino would become commissioner, saying: “This has never been discussed. However, the Fifa president and the Fifa administration will and must have leading roles in this entity.”

Sports.title: European nations ready to BOYCOTT World Cup as emergency meeting called over Gianni Infantino’s shameless plan
Sports.content:
EUROPEAN countries could BOYCOTT the World Cup if Gianni Infantino’s plan to flog a chunk of Fifa goes ahead.

Earlier today it emerged that Fifa are plotting to launch, and sell stakes in, a sister company that will preside over the World Cup and Club World Cup.



Selling off up to 20 per cent in a new Fifa Forward Enterprise could raise world football’s governing body more than £3bn from private investors, with plans having already received staunch opposition from UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Infantino, 56, would stand to make substantial sums in bonuses should the plan be successful – while he could also then move into a “commissioner” role world tens of millions with the new subsidiary once his final Fifa term comes to a mandatory end in 2031.



Uefa have already penned a furious response to the plans, with a statement reading: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. Uefa takes it extremely seriously.

“So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.



“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa’s to sell.”

According to Sky News, Uefa nations are set to discuss a World Cup boycott in opposition to Fifa’s plans.

Member associations will meet virtually for an emergency summit this week, with a possible boycott on the agenda.

SunSport understands that the FA were not previously aware of Fifa’s plans.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Various football associations met with Fifa on the eve of the World Cup final earlier this month, but these plans were not discussed.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin has already been critical of Infantino’s Fifa in recent weeks, having expressed his fury at the way in which Folarin Balogun‘s red card suspension was lifted during the World Cup, following a conversation between the Fifa president and Donald Trump.

Ceferin had attended the tournament’s opener, notably in Mexico, but opted to snub the final.

There is also a Trump connection with regards to the Fifa Forward Enterprise project.



Thrive Capital is understood to be the leading bidder, with its CEO Joshua Kushner the younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Infantino has responded to criticism, insisting that the plans will allow Fifa to offer more funding to member associations.

The under-fire president said: “Our next stage of growth needs a structure built for it, one where the commercial side of the game operates as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world.

“Every Fifa Member Association should have an opportunity to seek a fair share of the available funding to shape its own future, deciding for itself rather than relying on others. This is about the democratisation of football worldwide.”



Oppositing the plans, UK PM Burnham wrote on X: “Let me say this very directly.

“Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.

“Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”



It’s claimed that member associations will have access to $20m (£15m) in funding between 2027 and 2030 – an increase from the current $8m (£6m).

Next year there is a Women’s World Cup scheduled to take place in Brazil.

Then there is a Club World Cup scheduled for 2029, although a host nation has not yet been decided.

The next men’s World Cup will go ahead across Spain, Portugal and Morocco in four years.

Even if Uefa nations all oppose Fifa’s plans, Infantino and Co only need to receive a majority vote from their 211 member associations worldwide in order to press ahead with their project.



But a full Uefa boycott would cause significant issues for Fifa, given European football’s strength and support.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The 2022-2026 World Cup cycle is said to have pocketed Fifa £11.3BILLION in its current format.

In a further bid to increase revenue even more, it is expected that the World Cup will eventually expand again, this time to 64 teams.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off the World Cup is terrifying… the Fifa boss makes Sepp Blatter seem relatively OK
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL is not, and should never be, for sale.

Gianni Infantino’s latest idea to sell the World Cup to private investors is nothing short of an attack on the beautiful game.



The World Cup is not Infantino’s to flog, and offering it up to the ultra-wealthy will only invite more of the dangerous outside influence we saw when the Fifa President appeared to bow to Donald Trump’s pressure this summer.

Fifa would undoubtedly have to ensure any outside investors are happy by increasing profits and revenue.



What that could look like is almost unfathomable, but early speculation is that the World Cup could be expanded and even played more often than every four years.

No matter what the end result is, interference from the outside seems inevitable.



Perhaps the most terrifying part of Infantino’s new masterplan is that he claimed it would, “unleash the commercial potential” of football.

The same football that is set to bank Fifa over £11BILLION for the last World Cup cycle from 2022 to 2026.

Does that sound like an organisation that needs more money?

Infantino is constantly pushing the boundaries of what is acceptable and it is time for fans to finally let him know he has gone too far.



Uefa have already slammed Infantino and said his latest proposal “crosses a line” – just three weeks after they claimed that line was crossed when Folarin Balogun‘s red card was overturned.

In all honesty that line was surpassed a long time ago.

With each outlandish blueprint Infantino lays out, football is becoming more and more unrecognisable.



The average fan is being priced out of going to games, player welfare is being thrown to the wayside and the wallets of the elite are brimming at the same time.

Fifa will insist that this influx of cash will help the 211 national associations by giving them a financial boost.

Sure, a handful of smaller nations might thrive with a £15m handout, but the cash is unlikely to trickle down into grassroots football for the most part.

While that £15m pales in comparison to a potential £48m-per-year salary Infantino could reportedly bank if appointed “commissioner” of his new-fangled company.

If Infantino continues to get his way, football’s soul will be ripped away and so will the reason we all love watching it.



Remarkably, we are getting close to viewing Sepp Blatter as the lesser of two evils.

Sports.title: Son of Man Utd and England legend finally lands new club and admits ‘my career’s gone full circle’
Sports.content:
TOM INCE has completed a free transfer to Tranmere Rovers in a “full-circle” move.

The veteran winger, son of former Manchester United and England star Paul Ince, has penned a two-year deal with the League Two side.



Ince, 34, had been a free agent since it was announced in May that Watford would not be renewing his contract.

He now links up with his new club, and could be in line to make his debut this Saturday as they host Rochdale in the Carabao Cup preliminary round.



Upon completing the move back to Merseyside, former Liverpool starlet Ince told Tranmere’s club media: “It’s a great feeling, bit full circle for me. I’m looking forward to it.

“It’s always great when you come to a club like this. The good thing about it for me is that I have that hunger and that desire still.

“I think that’s what’s allowed me to have the career that I’ve been able to have, the amount of games I’ve been able to play and the level I’ve been able to reach.”

Former England youth international Ince started at Liverpool, another of his dad’s former clubs, and made one first team appearance for the Reds.

Following a loan spell at Notts County he signed for Blackpool, going on to impress for the Tangerines and even playing for his dad during his final season.

Ince scored 33 goals in 113 appearances for the Bloomfield Road club, and spent the second half of the 2013-14 campaign on loan at Premier League side Crystal Palace.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Upon the expiry of his Blackpool contract in the summer of 2014, Ince sensationally turned down Inter Milan to sign for Hull City.

He has since played almost all of his football in the Championship; representing Nottingham Forest, Derby County, Stoke City, Luton Town, Reading and Watford in the second tier.

Ince did get one more crack at the Premier League, playing 33 times for Huddersfield during the 2017-18 campaign.

He still played relatively regularly at Championship level last term – scoring four goals in 27 appearances for Watford – and could represent something of a coup for League Two Tranmere.



Rovers boss Darrell Clarke said: “Tom is a player who brings real quality and experience to the group. He’s played at a very high level throughout his career.

“He’ll give us creativity, composure and versatility in the final third, while his experience will be invaluable to some of our younger players and we believe he’ll be an excellent addition to what we’re building here.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino plotting shameless plan to SELL World Cup as furious Uefa blast ‘it’s not Fifa’s to sell’
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino is plotting an outlandish move to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The scheme, which would involve forming a company to control the World Cup and Club World Cup and potentially earn Infantino tens of millions of pounds, has already been blasted by Uefa.



European chiefs have launched a furious statement saying the idea “crosses a line”, adding that football is “not Fifa’s to sell”.

Potential investors have reportedly been briefed on the plot that would also see each of Fifa’s 211 member associations handed a £15m share of the company that they could choose to sell themselves.



According to The Times, figures close to Donald Trump’s administration are amongst those consulted about the plans.

Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group and JP Morgan is set to be Fifa’s financial advisor for the project.



Kushner, 41, is the younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Fifa would assume the majority ownership of the company, with private investors owning up to 30 per cent initially – costing them billions of pounds.

The money-making plot could also see Infantino appointed as an effective “commissioner” of the company once his final presidential term ends.

Infantino is set to be re-elected unopposed until 2031.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Reports have suggested that a commissioner role could carry an annual salary worth around £48MILLION.

The blueprint would likely drive Fifa – currently a non-profit organisation – to focus more on commercial revenue due to outside pressure from investors.

That could see the World Cup expanded from 48 teams to 64 and prioritising host nations based on their commercial potential.

There could also be pressure to hold the tournaments more often than every four years to increase revenue.



The Times report that Fifa’s 2022-2026 World Cup cycle is expected to have raked in £11.3BILLION in its current format.

A Fifa statement read: “Fifa is always on the lookout for innovative projects that can boost the development of football around the world and is always open to reviewing proposals submitted to it. We are starting a consultation process.

“As the Fifa President stated on July 18 during a meeting with all Fifa member associations, the priority now is to, ‘unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that Fifa has,’ after Fifa World Cup 2026 success.



“Fifa makes its decisions democratically, and a proposal that Fifa has received and is currently reviewing will soon be presented to the 211 Member Associations and the Fifa Council, who will be the sole final decision-makers on the matter.”

The project has already received major backlash, including the stern statement from Uefa. It read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. Uefa takes it extremely seriously.

“So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

This battle is the latest in football’s ongoing civil war that could tear the game apart.



UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin sensationally boycotted the World Cup final in New Jersey following the Folarin Balogun row.

Uefa branded the postponement of the ban “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable” and warned Fifa it had “crossed a red line”.

The controversy intensified after the US president revealed he had spoken to Infantino about Balogun’s case before the decision was made.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister employ private security after Argentina’s heated World Cup win vs England
Sports.content:
LISANDRO MARTINEZ and Alexis Mac Allister had security on patrol at their houses after Argentina’s World Cup win against England.

Private security firms were on site at the homes of the Manchester United defender and Liverpool midfielder in the North West.



Security personnel were present for two days with emotions high after England‘s 2-1 semi-final loss.

Argentina defender Martinez clutched a banner that read ‘The Falklands are Argentina’s’ while Mac Allister was nearby during celebrations with the bedsheet visible.



Cristian Romero and his former Tottenham team-mate Giovani Lo Celso also held the sign aloft, but the wantaway Romero could leave Spurs this summer.

No attempts to vandalise Martinez’s or Mac Allister’s properties were made and United were not involved in arranging the security detail for Martinez’s residence.



A mural of Marcus Rashford in Withington, Manchester was defaced after he missed a penalty for England against Italy in the European Championship final in 2021.

Martinez has developed a cult following since he joined United in July 2022 and their matchgoers have chanted “Argentina” in support of their Argentinian players over the last 25 years.

After Argentina won the 2022 World Cup, United fans welcomed Martinez back to Old Trafford by unfurling an Argentina flag in the Stretford End.

Mac Allister’s success in 2022 was similarly celebrated by Brighton, his club at the time. Seagulls supporters made homemade banners in tribute to the Argentine.



United’s and Liverpool’s fanbases are renowned for their lack of enthusiasm concerning the England national team.

A ‘We’re not English, we’re Scouse’ banner is frequently seen at Liverpool matches while a ‘United>England’ banner is permanently pinned up at Old Trafford.

United fans started chanting ‘Argentina’ in solidarity with David Beckham after his red card against the South American side in the 1998 World Cup.

A number of clubs have expressed an interest in the 25-year-old, namely Juventus, Roma and Como, as per i News. All three are pursuing are loan deal, with either an obligation or option to buy included, despite United preferring a straight sale.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham delivers passionate World Cup defence in face of FIFA plan to SELL competition
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham delivers passionate World Cup defence in face of FIFA plan to SELL competition

FIFA have been widely criticised for their plan to auction off a share in the World Cup to private investors and Prime Minister Andy Burnham has now had his say in a strong statement

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has hit back at FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has torn into FIFA for being ‘sell outs’ amid their plan to sell a share of the World Cup.

‌



World football’s governing body has unveiled a new plan to auction off a share in the competition to foreign investors - a plot that has been met with widespread criticism.

‌



Among the critics is UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Talking to social media, he wrote: “Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

‌



“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words READ MORE :

PM Burnham is not the only one to have hit out in the midst of FIFA's latest plan. European football's governing body UEFA have also had their say.

A statement read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross.

‌



“UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

Meanwhile, the Football Supporters' Association (FSA) released a scathing assesment. A statement on Tuesday read: “Many supporters came home from the World Cup believing FIFA couldn’t do much more to ruin everything we love about football’s greatest tournament. Less than two weeks after the final ball was kicked, they’ve shown they can always find a new low.

‌



View 2 Images Trump's administration have already been told about FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

“Like so many across the game, we are furious. We will examine the detail as it emerges, but we will do everything in our power as fans to fight back against the long line of decisions made that seriously threaten the future of football for short-term commercial gain.

“This cannot become another step in Gianni Infantino’s attempt to reshape football without regard for supporters or the wider game. We fully support UEFA’s statement. Every governing body, national association, league, club, supporter and stakeholder now has a responsibility to stand together and protect the future of our game.”

‌



FIFA have already issued their official plan. They confirmed that they intend to increase funding to over $10 billion (£7.49 billion). That funding would then be available to all 211 associations that are members of FIFA.

FIFA would remain as majority stakeholders of the World Cup, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations receiving a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

Sports.title: Argentine Premier League stars 'employ private security' after heated England win
Sports.content:
Argentine Premier League stars 'employ private security' after heated England win

Argentina reached the 2026 World Cup final with a controversial victory against England and it appears that some stars playing in the Premier League have stepped up their security measures in the aftermath

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister after Argentina's World Cup final defeat (Image: Getty Images)

Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister decided to bolster their home security in the aftermath of Argentina’s dramatic World Cup win against England. The South American nation reached the final earlier this month with a late, turnaround victory against the Three Lions.

‌



Anthony Gordon had given Thomas Tuchel ’s men the lead, only for goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez to turn the game on its head. Argentina players were criticised in the aftermath for celebrating with a banner declaring that the Falkland Islands were Argentinian, while their physical approach to the game was also a sticking point.

‌



And it appears that some of the players currently playing in the Premier League stepped up their security at their houses in the face of potential backlash. According to The Sun, both Mac Allister and Martinez employed private security firms to patrol their houses shortly after Argentina’s win.

‌



Those teams were present for two days following the game, albeit no attempts were made to vandalise either of the players’ properties. Manchester United are not thought to have had any involvement in Martinez’s arrangement for more security.

UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words READ MORE :

Argentina eventually lost the World Cup final against Spain - Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike securing victory for the European side.

Speaking after the World Cup final, Liverpool midfielder Mac Allister slammed rival fans for their responses. He said: "I have mixed feelings. It makes me a little angry because they have no basis for generating that hatred.

‌



“They say we're arrogant but maybe it says more about the people who say those things than about us. We have always been respectful to our opponents."

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez also stepped up security at his UK home (Image: Getty Images)

Taking to social media, he added: "Let's cry, because we're Argentinians and we always want to win. But after crying, let's get up, unite, and keep going, because this isn't over. And these past few days, my mum reminded me of a popular saying: 'If there's a rematch, don't be afraid.'

‌



"Finally, my eternal gratitude to our families, friends, those who do the silent work for this national team, and everyone who supports us throughout the year, in good times and bad. You are a huge part of who we are.

"Thank you to all Argentinians for every message of love and support. You don't know how important you are on this journey. And thank you also to those from other countries who send us messages mocking or rejoicing in our pain.

"Without meaning to, you help us feel more and more proud to be Argentinian every day. THANK YOU ARGENTINA!"

Sports.title: Vinicus Jr set to STAY at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest as Jose Mourinho pulls rank
Sports.content:
Vinicus Jr set to STAY at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest as Jose Mourinho pulls rank

Arsenal have been linked with a move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr, but the Brazilian is reportedly set to stay at the Bernabeu

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr will reportedly remain at Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal. (Image: Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has intervened and Arsenal target Vinicius Junior will not leave the club, according to reports. Sky Sports have claimed that the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager is keen to keep the Brazilian in the Spanish capital, scuppering Mikel Arteta's hopes of a landmark signing.

‌



The forward is into the last 12 months of his deal at the Bernabeu and uncertainty had been cast over his future at Madrid with the prospect of losing him on a free transfer. However, Mourinho has stepped in and Los Blancos will reportedly not sanction a sale while there is confidence that he will sign a new deal with the club.

‌



The Gunners had shown a genuine willingness to fund a move for the 26 year old after identifying the winger as a considerable upgrade on their current options, according to football.london.

‌



UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words READ MORE :

Arteta's side had been assessing the feasibility of pushing through a deal, with the Premier League-winning manager giving his blessing for the transfer to go ahead.

Arsenal had been on high alert regarding the prospect of snapping up Vinicius, with the two-time Champions League winner entering the final 12 months of his contract at the Bernabeu.

However, the Gunners will now be forced back to the drawing board, with Mourinho determined to keep his prized assets available as he prepares for his first season back at the helm.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It is understood that Vinicius and the Spanish giants are poised to enter fresh discussions, with the Brazilian international fully expected to put pen to paper on a new long-term contract.

Club president Florentino Perez is reportedly central to the negotiations and has made no secret of his determination for the forward to stay. Real Madrid head into the upcoming season aiming to topple rivals Barcelona from the top spot, after Hansi Flick's side cruised to La Liga glory with relative ease.

‌



Despite falling short of domestic honours, Vinicius remained integral to Real Madrid's attacking play, contributing 22 goals and 14 assists across all competitions. BBC Sport revealed earlier this week that the forward was open to staying at the club but wished 'to feel loved' with his new contract reflecting his significance to the side.

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr celebrates winning the 2023/24 Champions League with Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images Europe)

Mourinho's team have been active this summer following the signings of Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva on free transfers, while they secured Marc Cucurella and Denzel Dumfries from Chelsea and Inter Milan respectively.

‌



Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21 as they seek to successfully retain their top-flight trophy.

Christos Tzolis became the most recent summer acquisition after finalising his switch from Club Brugge. This summer's transfer window has proved a challenging market to navigate following the missed opportunities for Morgan Rogers and Jeremy Monga.

Chelsea and Manchester City moved swiftly to secure the two highly-regarded additions following Arsenal's public chase of the duo. Vinicius' standing could mean that any transaction for his services will surpass £100million.

Article continues below

Any transfer would almost certainly have implications for Gabriel Martinelli's future, with the club understood to be willing to entertain offers this summer.

Sports.title: Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery

Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni continues to be linked with a summer move to Manchester United as Michael Carrick looks to bolster his midfield options

View 2 Images Man Utd are interested in Real Madrid and France star Aurelien Tchouameni (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United could potentially sign Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni in August - if Rodri joins the Spanish giants by then. The French midfielder has reportedly signed a contract extension at Los Blancos, but the La Liga side are yet to confirm it, leading to hope at Old Trafford.

‌



The Red Devils are open to signing a third midfielder this summer after Casemiro's departure and Manuel Ugarte's serious injury during the recent World Cup. United have signed Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa so far, but Michael Carrick's squad lacks a specialist defensive midfielder.

‌



That has led to links with former Monaco star Tchouameni. It is understood that United have conducted background checks on the 26-year-old several months ago and are keen on a deal should he become available.

‌



Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Ruben Amorim admits to Man Utd mistakes and explains how sacking has changed him READ MORE :

And despite confusion over whether the No.8 has signed a contract extension at the Santiago Bernabeu, Real have been linked with a big-money move for Manchester City star Rodri and may need to drum up funds.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Spanish giants have stepped up their interest in the 30-year-old, who is into the final year of his City contract. Rodri has been offered fresh terms by the Blues, but the deal remains unsigned, and his future this summer remains uncertain.

‌



The Spanish World Cup winner has undergone surgery and is expected to remain out of action for a few weeks. When back to full fitness though - Real could make their move and sign him.

View 2 Images Rodri could hold the key to Man Utd signing Tchouameni (Image: Getty Images)

That means United could then have an opening to acquire Tchouameni in mid-August. Carrick's men have until the summer transfer window closes on September 1 to sign him.

‌



At City, new Blues manager Enzo Maresca has insisted that Rodri would 'be back with us' and that he was not concerned by the transfer speculation surrounding his star midfielder.

He said: "We have to say that around big players there are always speculation. I'm not worried about that, it's normal.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers

Chelsea have been linked with moves for veteran Premier League stars Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck and boss Xabi Alonso has spoken out on deals for the pair

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso took charge of his first Chelsea match on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - but hinted that the Blues want to add more experience. The Blues have been linked with moves for the veteran stars over the past few days.

‌



Reports have suggested that Henderson, 36, will be allowed to leave Brentford on a free transfer just a year after moving to West London. It has also been suggested that Chelsea are already in talks with Brighton regarding a move for Welbeck.

‌



Asked about potential deals following Tuesday’s 6-4 victory against Western Sydney Wanderers, new Chelsea boss Alonso remained tight-lipped.

‌



He said: “No, I'm sure that from today until the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them. It's going to be a hard task, but for sure we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance.

“We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team. For that we have an idea, we have a plan and let's see how we set it up until the start of the Premier League.”

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso left with easy transfer decision as Chelsea win Western Sydney Wanderers goalfest READ MORE :

Chelsea’s moves for Henderson and Welbeck are huge departures from their previous approach in the market. Having preferred to sign youth with promise in previous windows, the Londoners now appear to be prioritising experience.

‌



Chelsea have of course already been busy in the window this summer. Morgan Rogers arrived from Aston Villa for £117m earlier this summer, while Marco Palestra was signed from Atalanta.

Elsewhere, Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha arrived at Stamford Bridge on pre-agreed moves. The Blues have already earned considerable sums back, with Andrey Santos and Marc Cucurella having joined Manchester United and Real Madrid respectively.

View 2 Images Chelsea are interested in signing Jordan Henderson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Tyrique George has signed permanently for Everton following last season’s loan spell, while Alejandro Garnacho has been allowed to move to Aston Villa on loan. Another star who could leave before the end of the transfer window is striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old endured a difficult debut season with Chelsea, having netted on just three occasions. On the striker, Alonso added: “Every player that is involved is doing well, Liam as well. It was 60 minutes when he had to battle hard against the centre-backs, a good few lays off, so he's doing well and preparing for the season.

“I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football feeling good, and he's doing well.”

Sports.title: UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words
Sports.content:
UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors but European football’s governing body have fired back at that plot

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino faced severe criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA have taken aim at FIFA and said that football is ‘not theirs to sell’ in the face of their outrageous plan. Recent reports have suggested that world football’s governing body is planning on selling stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



The scheme could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn millions if a deal is rubber-stamped. The administration of US President Donald Trump has reportedly been consulted.

‌



And while the plan is still being mulled over by those within the organisation, it has not gone down well within UEFA.

‌



A statement from the Champions League organisers on Tuesday afternoon read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross.

Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return READ MORE :

“UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

‌



FIFA have already explained their plan in detail. In a statement, they confirmed that FIFA intends to expand football development funding to over $10 billion (£7.49 billion). That funding would then be available to all 211 associations that are members of FIFA.

View 2 Images Trump's administration have already been told about FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA would remain as majority stakeholders in the World Cup, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations would receive a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

‌



The Times has reported that one senior figure within the game has labelled FIFA’s plan as a "nuclear bomb" for the game.

FIFA President Infantino has regularly courted controversy this summer, particularly when it comes to the World Cup. Supporters took aim at him for the sky-high ticket prices during the tournament.

He was also criticised for his role in the decision to reverse Folarin Balogun’s ban for a red card. The American forward was initially suspended after being sent off, only for that decision to be reversed following a phone call from US President Trump.

Article continues below

On the criticism he faced, Infantino said : “You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all. To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness.”

Sports.title: Next darting superstar? Coates, 20, wins maiden PDC title
Sports.content:
Henry Coates sensationally won his maiden title at Players Championship 25 at Hildesheim in Germany.

The 20-year-old Englishman does not hold a PDC Tour card and came into the tournament as a top-up player from the Challenge Tour, but secured a sensational tournament win, beating Australian Damon Heta 8-4 with a 104.88 average in the 12-leg final.

"This probably won't sink in until next week," said Coates, who became the fifth player ever to win a PDC ranking title without a Tour card.

"Hopefully this is just the start. I've played for so many years and now the hard work and practice is paying off.

"Last time I played Damon it was my second ProTour event, just after I had won my first ProTour game, and I think he taught me a lesson beating me 6-0!

"I'm only a Challenge Tour player, but I'll take what I've got!"

Image: Gian van Veen lost in Jim Long in the round of 64

High-ranking Van Veen, however, was the victim of a 6-3 round of 64 shock defeat to Canadian Jim Long, with Long winning the last three legs to put out the World No 3 after the Dutchman handily beat Tom Sykes 6-3 in the opening round.

His countryman, Michael Van Gerwen, was able to make it through his opening matches, beating Adam Warner 6-0 and Darius Labanauskas 6-3 in the first and second rounds respectively, but Jeffrey De Graaf won five legs on the bounce to secure a brilliant last 16 victory.

Image: Michael Van Gerwen was knocked out of the round of 16 by Jeffrey De Graaf in Hildesheim

Elsewhere, Beau Greaves made a strong run to the round of 16 in her first tournament since winning the Women's World Matchplay in Blackpool, but fell 6-3 to German semi-finalist Niko Springer.

Sports.title: Mandhana fires Manchester Super Giants to victory over SunRisers Leeds
Sports.content:
Smriti Mandhana dazzled with an imperious 88no to fire Manchester Super Giants to a four-wicket win over SunRisers Leeds at Headingley.

SunRisers looked to have the upper hand after strong performances from Australian stars Phoebe Litchfield (31 off 26) and Annabel Sutherland (35 off 24) - aided by a brilliant cameo from captain Dani Gibson (18 off 6) - to give the home side a defendable score of 142, having lost just four wickets over their 100 balls.

The home bowling attack looked to have consolidated that prominent position with a brilliant second-innings spell which yielded four wickets for 10 runs, to leave the Super Giants reeling at 71-5 having been 61-2, but Mandhana held firm, with the opener reaching her half-ton from just 33 balls.

Image: Dani Gibson made 18 off 6 at the end of the SunRisers innings

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Headingley fans were stunned by Darcey Carter's drop catch.

Leeds looked to have taken the pivotal wicket 91 balls in, but Mandhana was dropped on the boundary by Darcey Carter on 71, and made no mistake with her remaining balls as she smashed two straight sixes to win the game for her side with five balls remaining.

The win preserves the Super Giants' unbeaten record, putting them second with 10 points in the Hundred table, while a second loss for the SunRisers leaves them fifth on four points.

Sports.title: Scandinavia retains Goodwood Cup crown after eventful race
Sports.content:
Scandinavia confirmed his superiority over Trawlerman to defend his Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup title in fine style at Goodwood.

Aidan O'Brien's son of Justify and his John and Thady Gosden-trained adversary had served up a thriller in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and another titanic tussle looked on the cards on the Sussex Downs.

Sent off the 6-5 favourite, Ryan Moore was always hot on the heels of Trawlerman who headed affairs in the hands of William Buick, in a race that had early drama when Amiloc unshipped Hector Crouch leaving the stalls.

Amiloc would again play a key role after Buick had set sail for home heading downhill into the straight and with the two Ascot rivals knuckling down for another battle, the loose Amiloc cut across the pair, checking Trawlerman's momentum and allowing Scandinavia to scorch clear.

He galloped on eight and a half lengths into the distance as Trawlerman finished second once again to his Ballydoyle foe, with Roger Varian's Rahiebb third.

"I'm delighted, I'm thankful to everyone around him. He's a great horse, he's a real top stayer," said O'Brien.

"He's a high cruising speed, he relaxes and finds his momentum. Ryan said he finds the minute he starts asking him, he starts coming alive underneath him.

Image: Ryan Moore rode Scandinavia to Goodwood Cup success

"We were a bit worried coming to Ascot because we've never been two and a half (miles) and you're never sure until you do it.

"We felt he's really gone the right way since Ascot. It's a great race to win, very prestigious.

"It's great that Trawlerman came and all the horses were there, it's what we all want to see - win, lose or draw.

"We thought that Trawlerman was going to make it, we were hoping that he would so Ryan could just follow him as he did in Ascot.

"It was going to be very simple, was he good enough or not? Obviously there was a little bit of drama, Trawlerman was a bit slowly away and Ralph's (Beckett) horse (Amiloc) was loose.

"It was a bit eventful, but it was still a great race at a great track. It was a spectacle to watch and going two miles, you get a great chance to look at it and take it in."

Of Scandinavia's future, O'Brien added: "He's very sound, he loves what he's doing and the lads love having him.

"When you get a horse like this that can race year in, year out, that's what makes it special.

"They're very hard to find, impossible really. I would imagine he'll keep racing as long as he stays safe and sound.

"He could (emulate Yeats, four-time winner of the Gold Cup), he's a natural cruiser. He's easy to train, he's a great mind and as he's by Justify, he has that great rhythm."

Moore said: "It was nice for him to have a horse to follow all the way, he probably thinks he got beat!

"His stride never shortened, he just kept galloping all the way to the line - what more can you say?

"He likes fast ground, he's a high-class horse and hopefully there's a few more good days to come."

Kaiya Fraser shines with Vintage performance

Kaiya Fraser produced a brilliant ride to land the Coral Vintage Stakes at Goodwood aboard the unbeaten Dr Rascal and celebrated the biggest victory of his career in the process.

The winning jockey had endured the nasty experience of being pulled from the saddle of the Oliver Cole-trained colt by the bite of a loose horse before remounting to win at Ascot earlier this month.

On this occasion the 23-year-old held his nerve to squeeze through a narrow gap on the rails on the inside of David Egan on Pikachu a furlong from home, delivering the son of Sottsass to land the spoils at 13-2 by half a length from the Aidan O'Brien-trained Haffner.

Favourite Al Hudaiba once again looked a difficult ride, with William Buick struggling to get him going before finishing a close third.

Fraser said: "It means everything, this is what we wake up for every morning.

Image: Dr Rascal claimed Group 2 gold at Goodwood

"I've put so much hard work in to get where I am today and all the people around who have helped me - my agent James Forrest and all the owners and trainers who put me up.

"I'm very grateful to them and I wouldn't be here if it wasn't for them."

He added: "You saw today, he had to get a push into the stalls because he obviously had that experience last time out where he got a bit nervous, but luckily he's a willing horse and he went in with a bit of encouragement and he got out and got the job done."

This was a first victory for Cole in a race his father Paul won three times with Putra (1996), Central Park (1997) and Strategic Prince (2006).

He said: "I was always quietly confident, he's a very good horse.

"I wasn't very nervous before the race which was quite a good thing because I have a lot of faith in this horse.

"He's a very fast horse… another unlucky run really because he got loose before Ascot and then he's just got mullered coming up there in the straight and he's still won.

"We'll probably look to the Dewhurst or something like that; he's got so much class and so much speed and he's very well bred, we're very lucky to have him in our stable.

"We're not used to these kinds of horses so back to the drawing board (for plans). The Royal Lodge probably not. I'll have to go away and have a think about it.

"It means a lot (to follow in his father's footsteps). My first complete year as a trainer, it means a lot. It's not just me, there's a big group at home that work so hard - I'm very proud of all of them."

The stewards did have a look afterwards, but found Fraser and Dr Rascal had gone through a legitimate gap on the inside of Pikachu.

Fraser said: "My horse slightly came off his line and I just had to straighten him up, didn't cause anything.

"I'm delighted, first Group winner - in a Group Two on a very nice two-year-old, so I'm looking forward to the future."

Sports.title: Doyle: Opera Ballo the main danger to Bow Echo at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Our ambassador gives her verdict on a stellar renewal of the Sussex Stakes on Day Two of the Glorious Goodwood Festival and provides her thoughts on the rest of the card.

Hard to oppose impeccable Echo in Sussex

It's difficult to make a cast-iron case against Bow Echo as he puts his unbeaten record on the line in the Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (4.10) at the Qatar Goodwood Festival on Wednesday.

George Boughey's colt was a brilliant winner of the Guineas before following up in the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot last month and has been delighting connections in his homework since.

He takes on the older horses for the first time but a handy draw in stall four as well as that eight-pound weight-for-age allowance strengthens his case to become the fifth three-year-old winner of this Group One in the last decade.

Front running Ballo could be hard to peg back

If there's one rival who could spoil the party in the Sussex Stakes it's Godolphin's Opera Ballo who ran a game race in the Queen Anne and could prove hard to peg back on a track that is better suited to front runners like him.

Charlie Appleby's colt has been building a serious profile with wins in the Group One Jebel Hatta in Dubai and a smooth success over Field Of Gold and subsequent Summer Mile winner Zeus Olympios at Sandown.

Aidan O'Brien's admirable Gstaad, who was second to Bow Echo at the Royal Meeting, is such a street fighter but lacks the turn of foot that Bow Echo possesses at that will probably be his undoing on the Downs.

Hannon filly sets standard in Molecomb

Richard Hannon and Sean Levey hold some strong chances at Goodwood this week but none more appealing than Pershaada in the Group Three Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes (3.35) on Wednesday.

This daughter of Persian Force is already a course and distance winner, landing a novice in May before running a big race in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot. She was little more than two lengths behind Victorious that day, finishing second in her group, and that form entitles her to plenty of respect in this field.

I'd love to see Rebecca Menzies win a big race like this with her unbeaten Adonius who has been kept fresh since extending his unbeaten record in the Lily Agnes at Chester and has speed to burn. It would also be nice to see Archie Watson's Flight Signal get back to the promise he showed on debut after struggling in the Norfolk Stakes.

Fabulous Flora the one to beat in Oak Tree

Flora Of Bermuda put her Royal Ascot disappointment firmly behind her in the Group Three Summer Stakes at York this month and can follow up in the Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes (3.00) at Goodwood.

Andrew Balding's course winner can take the step up to seven-furlong in her stride with a good low draw in her favour in this Group Three and can confirm this season's Newmarket form with market rival Sayidah Dariyan. She wasn't beaten far in the Group One Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot but whether she will see out seven-furlongs as well as Flora Of Bermuda is open to question.

Simon and Ed Crisford's Zanthos does have top class form at this distance having won the Group Two Rockfel Stakes at Newmarket last year but she needs to bounce back from her flop in the Commonwealth Cup with a tongue tie on for the first time.

Longer trip looks ideal for Infraad

I'm hoping my husband Tom (Marquand) can make a winning start on Wednesday in the Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap (1.50) when he partners William Haggas's smart Ghaiyyath colt Infraad.

A Pontefract novice winner, he looks ready for this step up to a mile and a half after making a promising handicap debut against more seasoned opposition at Chester a few weeks ago.

The handicapper has left him on the same mark of 90 which can give him the edge over a competitive field including Harry Eustace's Nottingham scorer Bay Royale - a taking son of New Bay who may just find more in a first-time tongue tie.

Moore booking catches my eye in finale

The closing HKJC World Pool Handicap (5.40) is wide open but the booking of Ryan Moore for Crimson Spirit can prove decisive.

Dan and Claire Kubler's five-year-old - a good second at Newmarket last time - doesn't have the best draw in stall 10 but won a big field handicap over course and distance back in May and remains fairly treated off his higher rating.

Likely favourite Bobby Bennu represents top trainer Roger Varain but hasn't won on turf for a long time and has produced his best recent form on an artificial surface. A three-pound rise makes this a tougher task so I'm happy to seek out some value with Crimson Spirit.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Why has Hamilton received so many penalties and what have they cost him?
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has received four penalties from the stewards in the last three Formula 1 race weekends - an unusually high number for any driver over such a short period.

After his latest penalty in Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix for speeding in the pit lane, Hamilton stated on the radio that the stewards are "handing out penalties like crazy".

The result was that Hamilton lost further crucial points in the title race, and he now trails Kimi Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, so have the penalties been justified?

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

British Grand Prix - false start

Finishing Position: Third

Points lost: Likely none

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New angles of Lewis Hamilton's false start at British GP

Hamilton was handed a five-second time penalty for jumping the start at the British Grand Prix when he was deemed to be creeping forward before the lights went out.

He went on to finish third, perhaps fortunately after knocking down his pit mechanic at a late pit stop, so the penalty likely did not impact his result. Hamilton considered the penalty harsh.

"We talked in the drivers' briefing the fact that they're inconsistent with this stuff. Drivers in the past have moved and not been penalised," he said.

"We discussed that, as long as you're not moving when the last lights are on, you shouldn't be penalised. I wasn't out of my box. And they agreed. So they're looking into that for the future."

Belgian Grand Prix - causing a collision

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to six

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

Hamilton was given a five-second time penalty for being "wholly at fault" for colliding with George Russell on the opening lap of the British Grand Prix at Turn 5.

On the inside line, Hamilton understeered into Russell and was "unable to maintain sufficient separation" which led to the contact and Russell spinning into the gravel and out of the race.

But, Russell himself said the contact was a "racing incident" even though he came off worse.

Hamilton said: "Even the driver I collided with said that it was just a racing incident. I think that one was not needed. But that cost me a lot of points."

Hamilton benefited from pitting and serving his penalty under a Virtual Safety Car, but without the penalty he would almost certainly have been on the podium rather than finishing fourth.

He may even have had a fighting chance of victory given his team-mate Charles Leclerc was only overtaken by race-winner Antonelli with 10 laps to go. A battle with Leclerc was definitely on the cards for second.

Hungarian Grand Prix Qualifying - impeding

Starting Position: Fifth

Impact: Potential to lead race and fight for win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's was given a grid penalty for blocking Oscar Piastri in qualifying in Hungary

Hamilton was hit with a three-grid place penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri during the final part of Qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

After completing his final Q3 run, where he did not improve, Hamilton was not told Piastri was starting his flying lap, so effectively blocked the McLaren driver through Turn 1.

"That was really just unfortunate. I take responsibility for ultimately being on track. I should have looked in my mirrors," said Hamilton.

"But I thought everyone would have been at the end of the first lap. The information I got was right at the end. A communication error."

Hamilton was not happy that Ferrari sent himself and Leclerc out first for the last Q3 runs, which partly led to the impeding incident with Piastri.

He had qualified second and, with brand-new soft tyres, would have had a golden chance to take the lead on the first lap and potentially win the race. Instead, he started fifth and was penalised again in the Grand Prix.

Hungarian Grand Prix - speeding in the pit lane

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to three

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson analyses Lewis Hamilton's speeding in the pit lane that handed him a five-second time penalty

The final race before the summer break was not well executed by Ferrari and Hamilton, who endured a difficult time after being overtaken by Max Verstappen after the first round of pit stops.

But Hamilton was still potentially on course for second until a Virtual Safety Car with 13 laps to go led Ferrari to pit for new fresh tyres.

In the pit lane, Hamilton exceeded the 80kph speed limit by 0.1kph as he was eager to beat Antonelli on the merge between pit exit and track.

It was a driver mistake but Hamilton thought, with hindsight, he should not have pitted and would have been third without the stop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

"The call came literally just before the pit lane entry and I didn't have time to debate and you've got to trust the decision that has been taken," he told Sky Sports F1.

"In hindsight, my tyres were totally fine. I was probably going to lose out to Max but I think I could have kept third at least. Then just opened up the door to obviously the penalty that I got in the end."

Hamilton: I can't give stewards any reason to penalise me

Apart from the Belgium collision with Russell, all of Hamilton's penalties are hard, or impossible, to argue against. He has probably only lost six points from the in-race penalties but the impeding in Qualifying at the Hungaroring was the most detrimental.

Ferrari had great pace in Budapest and track position is king, so a good start on softs from the front row of the grid likely would have seen Hamilton in the lead.

His raw speed has been very strong recently, too, so victory was possible on Sunday and he would have been less than 40 points behind Antonelli.

Ferrari and Hamilton must cut out these unforced errors if they want that record-breaking eighth world drivers' title.

"I'll work hard to try and come back. There's still a lot of positives to take. I'm going to try and make sure I don't give them any reason to penalise me," said Hamilton.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr set to stay at Real Madrid - what next for Arsenal?
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior will be staying at Real Madrid beyond this summer, Sky Sports News has been told.

The Spanish club have no intention of selling him and are confident he will agree a new contract.

This is despite the interest of Arsenal, who are monitoring his situation closely with a year remaining on his current deal.

On Monday, Sky Sports News broke the news that further talks over his future between Real and his representatives will take place this week. That is with the intention of making progress on a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu.

New manager Jose Mourinho is understood to value Vinicius highly and wants him to remain one of his top Galacticos.

What does Vinicius' future mean for Arsenal, Barcola & Diomande?

Sky Sports News' Dharmesh Sheth:

"Real Madrid are in a bit of a sticky situation because Vinicius Jr has only got one more year left on his contract. In six months from now, he could sign a pre-contract agreement with anyone outside of Spain. Then he could join any club for no money at all next summer.

“If you think about the valuation of the player, we think he is about £137m. That’s a large amount of money to forgo. However, they are confident he will sign that new deal.

“[The Diomande deal is] unaffected. I don’t think this has anything to do with Vinicius Jr at all. I suppose they may have used it to put pressure on Vinicius. He [Diomande] plays on both sides. There’s a situation where Yan Diomande can play on the right, Vinicius Jr signs his new contract and plays in his preferred position on the left, and Kylian Mbappe through the centre.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande says he is fully focused on the World Cup despite transfer speculation, but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger.

“As far as Diomande is concerned. He is continuing to train with RB Leipzig while talks with Real Madrid continue. Our colleagues from Sky in Germany are saying that the training is not that strenuous because they want to protect him. There is a feeling this deal is pretty close.

“There is a gap in valuation, but not so big that it’s insurmountable. It seems as if it is a one horse race because Paris Saint-Germain have publicly pulled out.

“Arsenal will continue to keep an eye on Vinicius Jr’s situation still. He hasn’t signed that new contract yet. As it stands, he has a year left on his contract. That’s why they are exploring the conditions of a possible deal.

“How Andrea Berta does his business at Arsenal is very clear. It’s not about one target and then the risk of that target not coming. They try to get their ducks in a row with three or four deals. Get as far down the line as they can with as many targets as possible, and then decide which player they are going to go for.

“One of those players is Bradley Barcola. He’s intimated to PSG that he’s not going to sign a new contract. That’s primarily because in the biggest games last season, he was on the bench. He doesn’t want to go through that again. It looks like he could become available for a transfer. Liverpool are interested as well and we think PSG will initially value him at £145m.”

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas:

The situation regarding Vinicius Junior has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest and further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms.

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.
