Sports.title: Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton
Sports.content:
Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton

An investigation has now been launched into Saltburn’s 2nd XI cricket match with Norton in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League

View 2 Images A village cricket game is being investigated

Village cricket has been rocked by a cheating scandal after a fielder was accused of clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of the ball hitting the bat.

‌



Footage appears to show a slip fielder for Saltburn 2nd XI snapping his fingers just before his wicketkeeper takes a catch. The batter appears confused to be given out.

‌



After the clip circulated, people accused him of fooling the umpire into thinking the batter had edged the ball.

‌



Ben Mummery, who shared the footage on social media, said: "Click-gate has gone viral and I’m genuinely really happy it’s being exposed. Harshest possible punishment please. It’s not cricket."

England cricket icon says wife was left 'suicidal' over Azeem Rafiq racism storm READ MORE :

View 2 Images An investigation has been launched into Saltburn’s match with Norton after cheating allegations (Image: Saltburn CC)

‌



The incident happened in a match in the North Yorkshire and South Durham League (NYSDL) between Saltburn 2nd XI and Norton 2nd XI, while ­Saltburn were fielding.

League leaders Saltburn ended up winning by a huge margin of 159 runs at their home ground in North Yorkshire.

Rory Cotterill, who captained Middlesbrough CC’s 2nd XI in a 29-run defeat to Saltburn in June, has since claimed a similar situation occurred in that match. He shared a video online which allegedly showed the same player clicking his fingers.

Article continues below

The NYSDL confirmed it received a formal complaint regarding S­aturday’s game.

It said: “A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made.”

Saltburn CC has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

Unmissable in-depth analysis of all eight races on the second day of the Festival which stages the week's signature race, the Sussex Stakes

View 6 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: CANNES is entitled to a plea of mitigation following his Royal Ascot blowout and deserves another chance.

‌



A debut second to his stablemate James J Braddock at the Curragh last November, the son of Sea The Stars took the silver medal home from his return to action at Leopardstown in April, but went one better in handsome style at the Foxrock venue the following month.

‌



Joseph O’Brien then gave Cannes his handicap debut in the King George V Stakes punters bought into the plan - my selection went off the 7-2 market leader in a field of 19.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

His supporters were left out of pocket when Dylan Browne McMonagle’s mount returned in 14th place behind his Ryan Moore-partnered stablemate Enceladus - but there are excuses.

Despite the big field, the leaders didn’t go off at a breakneck pace and the race unfolded to favour those positioned nearer the front than the back, which is where Cannes found himself during the early stages.

The handicapper has left Cannes on an unchanged mark of 95 and that’s a rating that looks within range for a colt who has plenty more to offer, while the unstoppable form of his trainer’s team is another reason to be cheerful.

‌



Of the remainder, Hatteen , Infraad and, at bigger odds, Parisian Scholar are three-year-olds open to further progress who have a role to play.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 CANNES, 2 HATTEEN, 3 PARISIAN SCHOLAR

View 6 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



2.25 British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes: WILD BLOSSOM is a two-year-old filly of significant promise who should make full use of this drop in class.

The daughter of Mehmas - dam Duchess Rose didn’t win but is a half-sister to Queen Elizabeth II Stakes hero Bayside Boy - cost 300,000 guineas at the breeze-up sales in April before being sent to join Karl Burke by owners Wathnan Racing.

Making her racecourse debut in a four-runner novice stakes for fillies over five furlongs at Carlisle the following month, Wild Blossom could hardly have been more impressive, sent to the front by James Doyle inside the two-furlong pole before careering away to humble Crownbreaker by 10 lengths.

‌



Sent off at 7-1 for the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot, my selection completed in 10th, beaten just over four lengths, behind winner Victorious, with four of today’s opponents in behind.

But that effort merits an upgrade as subsequent events at the meeting showed the far side, where Wild Blossom finished third in a group of 11, was at a disadvantage to the stands’ rail. With her sights lowered to conditions-stakes level, Wild Blossom is expected to get back to winning ways before returning to Group company.

Fast Track, 14th in the Queen Mary before a runaway success at Beverley, is a strong candidate for the podium, along with Weatherbys Super Sprint winner Zigazig Ah and Hidden Gift.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 WILD BLOSSOM, 2 FAST TRACK, 3 HIDDEN GIFT

View 6 Images Simon Crisford: trains Newsboy's pick with son Ed

5.00 Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes - ZANTHOS hasn’t yet reproduced the form of her two-year-old season - but there’s no time like the present.

‌



Roll the clock back to the autumn of 2025 and the daughter of Sioux Nation, trained in tandem by Simon and Ed Crisford, was proving herself in a higher grade than the company she’s keeping today.

A debut winner at Newmarket in August, Zanthos was unexpectedly beaten at odds of 4-11 at Leicester a month later. But she left that form well behind when outpointing The Prettiest Star by half a length for the Group 2 Rockfel Stakes back at Newmarket on her final start as a juvenile. It’s no calumny against Zanthos to say things haven’t worked out so far this term.

Returning in Longchamp’s Poule d’Essai des Pouliches in May, Oisín Murphy’s partner finished ninth of 15 behind Diamond Necklace and, stepping back from a mile to six furlongs, she came back 16th of 22 in the Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot won by Venetian Sun.

‌



But seven furlongs on fast ground are the conditions that have shown Zanthos, fitted with a tongue strap, in her best light and the drop to Group 3 level will help her bid to bounce back. Flora Of Bermuda carries a penalty for her success in York’s Group 3 Summer Stakes 19 days ago but is feared most, ahead of Planet Seeker and Radiant Beauty.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ZANTHOS, 2 FLORA OF BERMUDA, 3 PLANET SEEKER

View 6 Images Kaiya Fraser: won on Adonius at Chester (Image: PA)

‌



3.35 Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes: ADONIUS is the choice to give Co Durham trainer Rebecca Menzies a winner at Goodwood with her first-ever runner at the track.

The son of Soldier’s Call is already the best horse dual-purpose trainer Menzies has handled on the Flat - and is still a long way from the bottom of the barrel.

Reputed to be full of spirit during his pre-training days, Adonius was gelded prior to his debut at Musselburgh at the beginning of April but channelled his energies in the right direction to score by seven lengths.

‌



Adonius had just a neck to spare over Rlasthope under a penalty in East Lothian eight days later but did enough to earn a trip to Chester’s May fixture, where he contested the curtain-raising Lily Agnes EBF Conditions Stakes.

Again in front from flagfall under Kaiya Fraser, my selection took his record to 3-3 with a length-and-a-quarter dismissal of Hickory Lad.

Menzies resisted the temptation to go to Royal Ascot with Adonius, whose train-to-catch way of doing things will be well suited to the South Downs as he moves up to Group 3 level, and her patience can yield its reward.

‌



Pershaada, Ruler’s Pride and El Floridita were all beaten in different races at the royal meeting but warrant respect, all the same.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ADONIUS, 2 PERSHAADA, 3 EL FLORIDITA

View 6 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

‌



4.10 Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes: BOW ECHO has yet to taste defeat and is expected to take the score in his private battle with Gstaad to 3-0.

A perfect 3-3 as a two-year-old - he won a Newbury maiden, Haydock Park’s Listed Ascendant Stakes and the Group 2 Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket - the Night Of Thunder colt went into his winter quarters as one of the leading candidates for the 2,000 Guineas.

Bow Echo was an uneasy 9-2 chance on the big day, despite one upbeat bulletin after another from trainer George Boughey in the lead-up to the Rowley Mile test on the first Saturday in May.

‌



In the event, Billy Loughnane’s partner defied the market drift, coming from the back of the field to lead at the furlong pole and holding Gstaad by two and three-quarter lengths at the line, the pair a whopping eight lengths clear of third home Distant Storm.

Bow Echo went off at 5-6 to confirm that superiority over his Aidan O’Brien-trained rival in the St James’s Palace Stakes and did so - but only by a short head.

The result suggests that the momentum is with Gstaad, but Bow Echo tended to over-race after being leant on by the runner-up leaving the stalls yet demonstrated another facet to his game in being able to win ugly.

‌



It’s not hard to share Boughey’s view that Goodwood’s contours will play to Bow Echo’s strengths and he receives the vote to remain unbeaten.

Ten Bob Tony and Opera Ballo, first and third in the Queen Anne Stakes at the royal meeting, are taken to duke it out for the final place on the podium with the returning Zavateri and the top-class if quirky Never So Brave.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 BOW ECHO, 2 GSTAAD, 3 OPERA BALLO

‌

5.00 Coral Charlton Handicap: UNDER THE TWILIGHT was narrowly denied at this meeting 12 months ago but compensation is at hand.

The Michael Blake-trained mare went under by a neck to Dubai Treasure in the handicap for fillies and mares over course and distance, having scored at Windsor on her previous start. Under The Twilight then met with defeat on her next 10 starts but was back in business on Thameside 16 days ago.

‌



Sent off at 6-1 in a field of 12, Harry Davies’ mount came from the rear of the field to beat Amazonian Dream, who went one better at the track a week later, by a length and a half.

That success was gained from a British Horseracing Authority rating of 73 and Under The Twilight is 5lb higher in the handicap today.

But even that revised figure of 78 is 4lb beneath the mark from which she suffered last year’s near-miss, so the weights and measures point to another bold show.

‌



In a wide-open affair, Velvet Rhythm, French Affair, Lipsink and Calling A Star just four horses who merit a second glance.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 UNDER THE TWILIGHT, 2 VELVET RHYTHM, 3 CALLING A STAR

View 6 Images James Owen (second right) trains Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

‌



5.40 HKJC World Pool Handicap: GOLDMOYNE has been a gold mine for punters since joining James Owen and another good run is on the cards.

The ex-Irish six-year-old son of Galileo Gold has won six of his 19 outings for the Newmarket trainer, the most recent success coming on Polytrack at Lingfield Park in March.

Goldmoyne has made the frame in five of his seven races since then, but that doesn’t mean the British Horseracing Authority handicapper has caught up.

‌



Two starts ago, my selection ran down the centre of the course to finish second to Royal Zabeel at Newmarket, where the winner was favoured by being stationed towards the far side. And his third, beaten two heads, behind Northern Express at York 19 days ago was another fine effort against a course specialist who was cashing in on a falling mark.

Hardly a day goes by without Owen saddling a winner, and jockey Mason Paetel’s 5lb claim is another plus. Bobby Bennu, Crimson Spirit and Zarathos are at the top of a long shortlist.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 GOLDMOYNE, 2 BOBBY BENNU, 3 ZARATHOS

Sports.title: Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Goodwood on Wednesday on ITV
Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Goodwood on Wednesday on ITV

The in-form tipster hopes to continue his run of winning selections on day two of Glorious Goodwood when he has three tips including Ban Royale in the opener

View Image Steve Jones with his picks for Glorious Goodwood on ITV

Make it pay with Bay on day two of Glorious Goodwood. BAY ROYALE (1.50) has shown heaps of promise in three novice and maiden races. He now makes his handicap debut and he looks to have been handed an attractive weight.

It’s hard to understand how he is priced up at much bigger odds than both Hatteen and Infraad, considering he was much too good for both rivals on his return to action at Nottingham in May.

He couldn’t quite follow up under a penalty when runner-up – again at Nottingham – but he bumped into smart prospect Knights Charge and the front pair were well clear of the rest.

Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

A two-month break since that run should have done him some good and Harry Eustace’s well-bred three-year-old should enjoy the step up to 1m4f for the first time. Have 1pt each-way at 10-1.

Sports.title: Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’
Sports.content:
Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’

Trawlerman was practically stopped in his tracks by the riderless Amiloc in the straight before Scandinavia completed an impressive victory in the Group 1

View 2 Images Scandinavia chases the loose Amiloc at Goodwood (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

A loose horse caused chaos in the £500,000 Goodwood Cup after getting in the way ‘in the most important part of the race’ on Tuesday.

‌



The 2m Group 1 was supposed to produce a rematch between Ascot Gold Cup first and second, Scandinavia and Trawlerman, the horse who trains in special goggles to protect his eyes from the sun.

‌



Yet there was drama from the outset as first Trawlerman anticipated the start to burst out of the gate half a length in front of the rest. Then Amiloc lost his rider Hector Crouch who, after a valiant effort to stay in the saddle, was dumped on the turf.

‌



The riderless Amiloc decided to race ahead of the field, with Trawlerman kept a safe distance back leading the rest of the field.

But as soon as William Buick launched his bid for victory, Amiloc came right across the front of him, forcing the jockey to take evasive action to avoid a collision. With momentum lost, Scandinavia forged clear to win by eight and a half lengths.

Describing the interference afterwards, Buick said: “It’s significant. It’s hard to say how significant. He got in the way in the most important part of the race. It definitely had an effect.”

‌



View 2 Images Hector Crouch goes off the side of Amiloc (circled) as Trawlerman (far side) steals an advantage (Image: ITV)

Trainer John Gosden said: “When you’ve been crossed like that and checked, he’s not the type to turn around and start quickening. We got the worst of it and we went from being a length and a half in front to a length and a half behind. That’s racing.”

The stewards report said: “Approximately 2 furlongs out, the riderless AMILOC edged right-handed towards the rail resulting in the rider of TRAWLERMAN (IRE) having to take a check for a number of strides when placed on the heels of AMILOC, but after viewing a recording of the incident, it was found that no riding offence was involved.”

‌



After looking into the incidents at the start the stewards were satisfied that Amiloc was a runner “as the rider was mounted as the start was effected before AMILOC jumped left-handed, resulting in Crouch catching his leg on the starting stalls, causing him to become unbalanced and ultimately unseated shortly after the start.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The report added: “TRAWLERMAN (IRE), drawn 8, anticipated the start and accelerated the gate at the same moment as the start had been effected, thereby enabling the gelding to break quickly. Being satisfied that it was not caused through a faulty action of the starting stalls, no further action was taken.”

Sports.title: Man Utd learn Iliman Ndiaye asking price in transfer battle for Everton star
Sports.content:
Man Utd learn Iliman Ndiaye asking price in transfer battle for Everton star

Manchester United are considering a move for Iliman Ndiaye, who also has interest from Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal, but Everton are set to ask for a hefty transfer fee

View 2 Images Iliman Ndiaye is in demand (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Everton will demand around £70million for in-demand star Iliman Ndiaye amid interest from Manchester United and Al-Hilal. Ndiaye, 26, is a wanted man after a couple of eye-catching seasons on Merseyside.

‌



The forward is open to leaving Everton and his camp would encourage a bid from the Saudi Arabian side. But United are also in the running, with left wing among their priorities this summer.

‌



Michael Carrick's side have shortlisted Ndiaye and are tracking his situation. The Athletic report that Everton are aware of Al-Hilal's interest, although no talks between clubs have taken place.

‌



It's added that Everton are expected to ask for a fee similar to the £70million that Barcelona paid Newcastle United this summer for Anthony Gordon. Ndiaye also has three years left on his contract and the Toffees are in no rush to sell him.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks READ MORE :

Ndiaye has come to the forefront of United's options after Morgan Rogers went to Chelsea for £117m and Yan Diomande indicated that he wants to join Real Madrid. However, their search for a left winger isn't as pressing as other areas, with Marcus Rashford due to be integrated back into the squad after a season on loan at Barcelona.

‌



There have been claims that Everton would like to hand Ndiaye an improved contract in order to fend off interest, but he's rejected their proposals. The Toffees paid £15m for Ndiaye two years ago when he arrived from French giants Marseille.

The former Sheffield United star has scored 17 goals and provided three assists in 71 appearances for Everton. Ndiaye went to the World Cup with Senegal, starting one of their four games as they reached the last 32.

Is Iliman Ndiaye worth more than £70million? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Iliman Ndiaye impressed at the World Cup (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Despite playing 127 minutes, he came away with one goal and two assists. Prior to the World Cup, Ndiaye revealed that his ambition is to play in the Champions League. "You don't know where football will take you next," he told Sport Bible.

"As I've always said, I want to be the best player and to do that, you have to play at the top. I want to be playing at the top level. I want to be playing Champions League football."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory

Anthony Joshua was dropped twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga on Saturday night, but rallied to a stunning second round knockout in Saudi Arabia

View Image Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

A member of Anthony Joshua's team has brutally hit back at Simon Jordan after the talkSPORT presenter questioned the Brit's knockout victory over Kristian Prenga.

‌



'AJ' returned to the ring on Saturday night for the first time since being involved in a tragic car crash over in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion was dropped twice in the opening round by the Albanian, but sensationally rallied to a second round knockout victory. Joshua's remarkable win has guaranteed a date with long-time rival Tyson Fury - which is due to take place before the end of the year.

‌



Yet Jordan was rather sceptical of the end result, writing: “Not having that … #anthonyjoshua fight. Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how’s that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd. Something not quite right , all designed to rinse maximum amount of money …”

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jake Paul and Eddie Hearn team up in shock move to end heated rivalry READ MORE :

Sergey Lapin, Director of Team Usyk, has since brutally hit back at Jordan's remarks. Joshua teamed up with the Ukrainian's team prior to his bout with YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul back in December - and Lapin once again played a key role on Saturday night.

In an interview with Action Network, Lapin said: "What do I think of Simon Jordan’s comments? I suppose they also told Prenga to walk straight into a punch that weighed one and a half tonnes. Everyone is entitled to their own theories. I have a friend who still believes the Earth is flat and that space doesn’t exist. Personally, I’d rather discuss what actually happened inside the ring than someone else’s imagination."

Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss READ MORE :

Lapin was quick to turn his attentions to Joshua versus Fury, and is confident his man can secure a devastating knockout over the 'Gypsy King.' "Time certainly plays a role. It helps you recover, refine your game, and sharpen your timing. But time alone doesn’t win great fights," he said.

Article continues below

"When it comes to Joshua versus Fury, I genuinely believe AJ can knock Tyson Fury out. This is the kind of fight where one mistake changes everything. Both men have what I call a “red button”—one decisive shot capable of ending the night. The question isn’t whether the fight happens in one month or six. The question is who finds that moment first. That’s why I believe AJ can finish the fight inside the distance."

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return

Italy have finally ended a week of turmoil by appointing Roberto Mancini as Claudio Ranieri is hired as technical director - replacing Paolo Maldini

View 2 Images Roberto Mancini, who won Euro 2020, is back in charge of Italy (Image: getty)

Italy's manager search has ended with Roberto Mancini taking charge for a second spell - and Claudio Ranieri coming in as the country's technical director.

‌



Monday proved a pivotal day as Azzurri legend Paolo Maldini quit after only 16 days in the job after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from taking over the four-time World Cup winners. Some senior figures at the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) shied away from his appointment due to ties to a Russian betting firm.

‌



Pirlo was the third man to be eyed for the job after Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti both said no. Mancini is the fourth man they've gone after a finally a deal has been agreed with Ranieri sitting in a senior role.

‌



The FIGC president, Giovanni Malago, said on the appointment: “Mancini is the coach. I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson READ MORE :

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini and will oversee technical operations and elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. He's most heralded for leading Leicester to the Premier League title but has also managed Juventus, Roma and Inter Milan.

“I needed someone with whom I could share ‌the decision on the coach, because without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

‌



In hiring Mancini they bring back the last man to lead Italy to tournament glory, although either side of that they've been wholly disappointing. The former Manchester City boss replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession. He held the job from 2018 to 2023 and claimed Euro 2020 glory following a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley.

View 2 Images Italy have bought in Claudio Ranieri as technical director

Mancini ultimately presided over the Azzurri's world record 37-game unbeaten run, but couldn't qualify for the 2022 World Cup - losing to North Macedonia in a play-off - before resigning in August 2023.

‌



Italy became the first World Cup winners ever to miss out on three tournaments successively having not played at the finals since 2014, when they were knocked out in the group phase. That was also the case in 2010, marking a dire run since they claimed the World Cup in 2006.

Italy start their Nations League campaign on 25 September at home to Belgium before travelling to face Turkey three days later.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
