The campaign was funded by South African Tourism – the Department of Tourism’s official national marketing agency – as well as private-sector organisations such as the Tourism Business Council of South Africa (TBCSA) and Tourism Marketing South Africa (TOMSA).

In the ad, which was also posted on YouTube, Trevor showed off Mzansi as an idyllic holiday destination, complete with favourable weather, beautiful landscapes, wildlife and vibrant cultures.



He joked: “Still South African, still a comedian…I guess I am the only South African people can ask. Why not ask Black Coffee, Charlize, Elon…ok maybe don’t ask Elon”.

Trevor also mentioned the affordability of vacationing in Mzansi, which has been commended for its “five-star travel on a budget” offering.

He continued: “In South Africa, you can do a little bit of this or that. Whatever vacation you are looking for, South Africa has you. Don’t say we didnt tell you!”



Watch the ad below…

FREE SERVICES OR MULTI-MILLION PAY DAY?

Trevor Noah’s promotion of South African tourism has raised the question – who funded the campaign, and how much did he earn for it?



According to the Tourism Business Council of South Africa, Trevor offered his services at a “discounted” rate.

TBCSA CEO Tshifhiwa Tshivhenga told Moneyweb that the campaign had an overall cost of around R60 million, which would be spent on a rollout in the coming months.

Tshivenga said: “Trevor Noah is a globally recognised comedian and is an ambassador of South Africa. So it was a natural choice to continue with this campaign.



“He was keen from the outset and actually charged us less than half of what he would normally charge to be part of an ad campaign… However, we may rope in other South African icons in future campaigns, but the first ad with Noah really delivered for us in terms of reach,” he adds.

In 2023, TBCSA denied reports that it had paid Trevor R33 million to film a promotional video released at the time.

Tshivhenga told the SABC: “We have never come out and said we’re paying him R33 million. These were reports that came from the Parliament Portfolio Committee, which should be in a position to answer those particular questions.



He continued: “We did this deal with Trevor Noah. He is the talent for this, he got a fee and a very small amount to do this. As a star whose appeal is international, Trevor Noah is definitely not paid R33 million. That’s a myth, and those people who have said that they should be able to answer those questions.

Tshivhenga claimed that Trevor Noah actually “gifted” his services.

He continued: “We have a deal that is very straightforward. He’s a well-known brand in the world. And his fees were actually a gift to us for him to agree to do this.”



Trevor reaffirmed the organisation’s comments in an interview with 702.

World.title: FIFA stake sale plan sparks UEFA anger
World.content:
The world governing body wants to create a new commercial company called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). The new entity will manage broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing, licensing and the delivery of major tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup, FIFA Women’s World Cup and the expanded FIFA Club World Cup.

FIFA TARGETS BILLIONS THROUGH NEW VENTURE

With advice from JPMorgan, the new business is valued at $20 billion. It plans to sell up to a 20% non-controlling stake, which could raise around $4.2 billion.

The investment group is expected to be led by Thrive Eternal, a fund launched by Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital.



President Gianni Infantino believes the new structure will generate more than $10 billion for football development over the next four years.

Also read: Themba Zwane linked to FIFA World Cup match-fixing allegations

To gain support from its 211 member associations, the gorvening body has proposed a once-off payment of $20 million to each nation through a new FIFA Fast Forward Program. The governing body also insists it will retain full ownership of the company. Private investors will not have any influence over football rules, competitions or the international calendar.



UEFA REJECTS PROPOSAL

UEFA has strongly criticised the plan. The European governing body warned that the proposal could create serious divisions within world football.

Led by president Aleksander Čeferin, UEFA said the FIFA plan “crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross”. It also questioned the transparency of the proposal and demanded more clarity on who would benefit financially.

The organisation ended its statement with a strong message. It said the soul and governance of football are not for sale and insisted that no governing body owns the game.

World.title: Pretoria man accused of intentionally infecting lover with HIV appears in court
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A 47-year-old man accused of infecting his 38-year-old girlfriend with HIV is in custody.

He appeared before the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court, where his case was postponed to 3 August for obtaining bail information.

The man from Boschkop in Pretoria faces charges relating to attempted murder.

National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) spokesperson Lumka Mahanjana said his alleged crime dates back between October 2025 and June 2026, when the accused and the woman were in a relationship.

READ | SA receives 37,920 HIV prevention injections

During this time, the man allegedly lied about his HIV status, claiming he was HIV negative.

However, things later took a turn when the woman allegedly discovered antiretroviral (ARV) medication in the accused’s bag and confronted him about it, Mahanjana said.

“The accused allegedly admitted that he was HIV positive and informed her that he had intentionally infected her because he did not want her to be with another person. “On 25 July 2026, the complainant underwent an HIV test at a medical facility and was informed that she had tested positive for HIV,” she said.

According to Mahanjana, the matter was reported to the police and subsequently arrested at his residence.

World.title: Convicted rapist gave child R4 after ordeal
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A scholar transport driver from Mamelodi in Pretoria was sentenced to life imprisonment for raping a nine-year-old child.

The Pretoria Regional Court found that the 41-year-old man was guilty of the rape, saying he exploited the vulnerability of an unsuspecting child.

National Prosecuting Authority (NPA)spokesperson Lumka Mahanjana said the heinous crime dates back to June 2021.

In a statement on Tuesday, Mahanjana detailed how the man invited both the victim and her seven-year-old brother to his home for a visit.

This was after he had dropped off the victim’s brother at home after school.

The children heeded the request and told their mother that they were going to play outside, only for them to journey to the scholar driver's home, the statement read.

READ | 'It's rape' - Anti-GBV group alarmed as 300 WC girls aged 10 to 14 give birth

According to Mahanjana, when the two arrived at the man’s residence, he gave the seven-year-old boy money to buy tea bags from a nearby shop.

“When the victim insisted on accompanying her brother, [the driver] instructed her to remain behind. After the boy left, he locked the door, undressed himself and the child, and raped her,” she said.

Mahanjana said the scholar transport driver stopped the ordeal when the victim's brother returned and proceeded to threaten to kill the victim’s mother if they disclosed the ordeal.

“Before they left, he gave the children R4 to buy chicken heads,” she said.

The child only confessed about the heinous crime to her mother a month later.

READ | Dobsonville rape case postponed to 1 July

The man pleaded not guilty and denied committing the offence.

However, Mahanjana said the court found no substantial and compelling circumstances justifying a deviation from the prescribed minimum sentence and concluded that a life sentence was appropriate.
