World.title: Estonian schools struggle to fill math and primary‑class teaching jobs
World.content:
Schools are looking most actively — through public job postings — for mathematics teachers and primary‑class teachers, but English teachers are also in very high demand. The largest number of vacancies is in Tallinn and Harju County, but teachers are frequently missing in Lääne‑Virumaa and Tartu County as well.

In the Õpetajate Leht job listings, schools are seeking 147 education workers — 134 teachers and 13 special‑education or support staff.

There are 92 active postings in total. Although some advertised positions may already be filled, the data provides a good overview of which types of teachers are most needed in which municipalities.

Olga Selištševa, director of Tallinn Tõnismäe State High School, which is looking for four teachers, said the high demand is nothing new. "It was the same last year and the year before. It's an annual situation," she said.

According to Selištševa, the large number of people aspiring to become teachers may give the impression that many new teachers are entering schools, but in reality most who enroll in teacher‑training programs are already working in schools and simply want to obtain the qualification.

"New people aren't coming, and that's the problem," she said.

Tallinn Avatud Kool opened on September 1 in Tallinn, one of two new schools opening in the capital this year. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

By county, Harju County has the most vacancies, with 32 job postings. Lääne‑Virumaa is looking for 12 education workers, and Tartu County for 10.

Pärnu County and Järva County each have five openings, Ida‑Virumaa four, and Jõgeva, Põlva, and Valga counties three each. Rapla, Viljandi, and Võru counties each have two, and Lääne County has one vacancy.

By position type, the largest number of postings are for primary‑class teachers, with 34 vacancies. Among subject teachers, mathematics teachers are most sought after, with 26 postings.

Schools are looking for 19 English teachers and 15 music teachers. There are 11 postings for Estonian language and literature teachers, and four for Estonian language teachers.

Physics teachers are needed for eight positions and chemistry teachers for four, plus one combined physics‑or‑chemistry posting.

Among support specialists and positions related to teaching students with special needs, the most vacancies are for speech therapists, who are sought by 19 institutions.

In many cases, schools need more than one new teacher.

World.title: Infrastructure in Estonia surges while apartment construction falters
World.content:
Apartment building in Estonia is currently sluggish, while infrastructure is booming, says Tarmo Pohlak, board member of the construction company Nordecon.

Pohlak says that the many construction cranes currently visible in central Tallinn represent only the tip of the iceberg, and the decisions to build those buildings were often made long ago.

At the same time, major infrastructure projects are underway in Estonia: 45 kilometers of 2+2 road are being built on the Tallinn–Pärnu highway, and part of the Tallinn–Tartu highway is also out to tender.

Construction of Rail Baltic is ongoing as well, though it is not very visible to ordinary people in the cityscape. Based on current knowledge, Estonia will complete its entire section up to Ikla on the Latvian border, and the pace will be very fast until 2030. "There are very large volumes of concrete, earthworks and other materials," Pohlak said.

According to him, Nordecon is also building several national defense facilities deep in the forests, where the work volumes are quite large.

Pohlak says the economy is currently highly volatile, yet construction companies are required to adhere to fixed prices. "Someone made the comparison that if Eesti Pank says it cannot produce very precise forecasts, then construction companies, when submitting bids, must be able to foresee everything and factor it into their price."

"Reedene intervjuu": Tarmo Pohlak Autor/allikas: Ken Mürk/ERR

In the private sector, Nordecon is currently building two hotels — one in Viljandi and the other on the shore of Lake Peipus. "Both entrepreneurs have taken a big risk, and we are happy to build."

But when it comes to apartment construction, current volumes are incomparably smaller than before the COVID pandemic.

Developing commercial real estate is also difficult at the moment. "You have to believe you will have clients, or in the case of an office building, you must know who you are building it for. You have to secure an anchor tenant. Entrepreneur Urmas Sõõrumaa signed a contract with SEB Bank, which is a very large anchor, and thanks to that the major Talsinki Quarter project went ahead. It is a very large private investment in central Tallinn, but without the SEB contract, that plot would be silent today," Pohlak noted.

The new 'Talsinki' retail and residential area in central Tallinn. Source: Talsinki arhitektuuri loovad arhitektuuribürood Arhitekt 11 ja HGA, maastikuarhitektuuri autor on TajuRuum. Sisearhitektuuri kujundavad studio ARGUS (kodud) ja LÄVI (bürood). Ehitab Bildgren Ehitus.

The state is improving infrastructure, but practically no new large state building projects are coming, Pohlak said. The only known project is the Siuru Cultural Center in Tartu. There are some schools and kindergartens, but from the builder's perspective these are relatively small.

Pohlak recalled that in spring 2022, at the start of the war in Ukraine, a materials shortage emerged reminiscent of Soviet times. "I was on the client side then, walking around the site. One wall was insulated with one type of mineral wool, another with a different type, and a third with a third type. If you asked the main contractor why, they used whatever they could get at that moment. If nothing was available, work stopped. The price of rebar doubled or tripled overnight."

According to Pohlak, the building sector adapted to the situation, but now there are new problems. The situation in the Strait of Hormuz pushes oil and gas prices up and down. Many construction materials — and transport — are tied to oil and gas prices.

Pohlak noted that if all Ukrainian construction workers were to leave Estonia, the impact would be catastrophic. "Without foreign labor it would be very difficult, because there are not enough workers. And they are very capable."

Cranes building the Rail Baltica terminal in Tallinn. Source: Mait Ots/ERR

World.title: Ida-Viru County seeks tourism rebrand beyond Soviet-era 'ghost town' image
World.content:
Being adjacent to the eastern border and its distance from Tallinn mean Ida-Viru County has long been somewhat off the beaten track, attracting more niche types of tourism than other parts of the country.

One classic example of this is the former mining town of Viivikonna, famed for being a ghost town, though there are people living there again nowadays.

Local residents are often keen to move away from the old Soviet tag and embrace something new.

"We want to turn [Viivikonna] back into a holiday destination, with beautiful backyards. Perhaps in the future it could become an example of how to turn an ugly town into a beautiful settlement," Priit Orav, who has worked as a tour guide in the area for around 25 years, suggested.

Viivikonna as it is now has, thanks to its abandoned and eerie nature, long been a popular destination for visitors, tourists, and even filmmakers exploring new locations.

Ruined building in Viivikonna. Source: Chris Feichtner/Flickr

"I think there is already enough material about it on YouTube, and filmmakers from all over the world have been there. Now I think it is time to draw a line under it. We need to move on from this Soviet nostalgia. Right next door, beautiful private homes have been built or old ones have been renovated, and everything is already beginning to take on a European appearance," Orav explained, talking to "Vikerhommik".

The transformation process is already underway, and the larger buildings have largely been demolished, leaving only the former schoolhouse and a few smaller residential buildings.

These latter buildings are often being used as homes nowadays in any case, Orav noted. "What is left are smaller houses that were once built for four families. They have become homes for one or two families, with beautiful gardens. People do care about their surroundings."

In the quarter of a century Orav has worked as a guide in Viivikonna, he has conducted around 100 tours of the so-called ghost town, and so has seen the transformation at first hand. "I have seen this change and I have also seen the reaction of the local residents. They have for a long time been tired of the fact that so many people go there, and that the place has attracted the attention of social media around the world," he said.

The same can be said of the surrounding area. "I hope this place will develop into a quiet, nice settlement with low-density housing. Just 10 kilometers away is Sillamäe, which has also become very beautiful nowadays," Orav added.

The center of Sillamäe is an example of typical Stalinist architecture. Source: Visit Estonia/ Tauri Taal.

He also often conducts tours of Sillamäe, a nearby port town with notable neoclassical architecture dating mostly to the Stalinist era. "Of course, it has a Russian or Soviet 'accent', but that is exactly what people come to see, because there is no other city like it in Estonia. Now we just have to wait for the local residents of Sillamäe to grasp that the old town of Sillamäe is an attraction, and that the buildings and exterior façades ultimately need to be restored."

Other highlights include the beach at Narva-Jõesuu, downstream from Narva and a resort town. It is very difficult to find anything similar to Narva-Jõesuu elsewhere, Orav said, also bringing out the Aidu quarry, where a versatile water sports center has been established, as characterizing a new emerging trend.

"The Kiviõli ash hills have found their place, but the new rowing channel at Aidu and everything else around it, as well as the underground mine in Kohtla-Nõmme, are things that only we have; there is nothing like them elsewhere in Estonia."

Kiviõli hosts a notable motocross circuit, skiing can be done on some of the artificial slopes left over from mine tailings, and the forests of Ida-Viru County are home to a population of Siberian Flying Squirrels.

Ultimately what makes Ida-Viru County a special tourism destination is its natural beauty: Its vast array of rivers, lakes, the sea, forests, bogs, and wetlands, Orav concluded.

World.title: New ambassador to the US: I'm ready to run in presidential elections
World.content:
Incoming Estonian ambassador to the United States Hannes Hanso has said he would be willing to be a candidate at September's Estonian presidential elections, if asked.

Hanso, 54, until recently Estonia's ambassador to China, said he would make a good president if elected, adding more than one party has floated the idea.

"It is true that two or three parties have discussed my possible candidacy in various formats. Also in a broader circle. That is, in itself, a great honor for me," the newly appointed representative to Washington, told Vikerraadio's Uudis+ program Tuesday.

In response to the host's question about what his response would be if party leaders asked him to run for president, Hanso said: "What would I say? It would be tough for us to reorganize our family life once again, but I would definitely be ready. I have no doubt that I would be a good president of the republic."

Hanso noted his resume includes a stint as minister of defense (2015-2016). He has also served in local government, including as a mayor, and on local councils as well, and national politics as a past Riigikogu member, where he chaired the Riigikogu's foreign affairs and national defense committees at various times. He was also briefly an MEP (2019).

"If those are the experiences and competencies that are being sought, then as a citizen it would almost be irresponsible to say 'no,' if such a consensus could be built around me. To refuse to take on that responsibility. Then we would have to reshuffle our cards once again, and the children would also be very happy that they could finally live in Estonia again. In short, Hannes Hanso would not throw in the towel and would say 'yes'."

Hanso also said he does not like the situation which has emerged around Estonia's presidential election process and the upcoming election in particular.

Ballots being counted at the first round of the 2021 presidential election. Source: Erik Peinar, Chancellery of the Riigikogu

"The world is unstable and turbulent. We need some clarity, and people should be honest. If they have an ambition to become president, they should say so. Be a man and say it, or be a woman and say it: 'Yes, I am interested. I believe we all have a responsibility for these matters.' Standing behind a bush, hedging, or keeping the door open without saying anything – there is really no need for such fear. It is the greatest honor a person can have: to be the head of state, the country's leader."

Hanso was appointed Estonia's next ambassador to the U.S. in early June, replacing Kristjan Prikk, who is to become Estonia's ambassador to NATO later in the year. Hanso had been ambassador to Beijing up to his new appointment.

Hanso's declaration comes at a time when several other public figures have either been put forward by politicians as candidates, or declared their own interest in running. The first group includes Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, while former Defense League commander Riho Ühtegi is in the latter camp.

Estonia's presidents are elected by the Riigikogu in the first instance, with a majority of 68 at the 101-seat chamber needed, meaning cross-party support of coalition and opposition parties is required for a candidate to get voted in.

If three rounds of voting draw a blank, the process moves to the regional electoral college.

Nominations open for candidates on August 21, and close August 24. The Riigikogu voting rounds start on September 2.

Hanso was a member of the Social Democratic Party (SDE) from February 2009 until June 2019.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey deepen security, energy ties after PM’s Ankara visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq and Turkey agreed to deepen cooperation on security, energy, commerce, and the centerpiece Development Road project on Tuesday as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi wrapped up his first official visit to Ankara since taking office.

Following conversations with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the two sides agreed to speed up the development of the Development Road corridor, which connects Iraq’s Grand Faw Port to Turkey and then to Europe, while also working to finalize a comprehensive bilateral energy cooperation deal.

In a joint statement, Baghdad and Ankara stated that they would strengthen cooperation in water resources, energy, trade, agriculture, transportation, investment, defense industries, and education, describing the Development Road as a critical project for increasing regional connectivity, economic integration, and long-term stability.

The two nations also reiterated their commitment to strengthening security cooperation in the face of transnational threats.

Erdogan commended Iraq’s support for Turkey’s war against extremist organizations, and both sides agreed to strengthen information sharing and security cooperation to defend their borders and maintain regional peace.

The visit comes as Iraq wants to improve economic ties with neighboring nations while portraying itself as a regional transportation and logistics center, linking the Gulf to Europe via new road, rail, and energy infrastructure.

Al-Zaidi’s travel comes after recent trips to the United States and Iran, where Iraq inked investment, transportation, and energy deals as part of a larger diplomatic effort to attract international investment and diversify the economy beyond oil.

The two countries also agreed to improve the legal framework regulating bilateral ties by ratifying outstanding agreements, signing new cooperation instruments, and holding the fifth meeting of the Iraq-Turkey High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council in Baghdad at a later date.

On regional concerns, Baghdad and Ankara said they would continue to closely coordinate on Middle Eastern events, confirming Syria’s unity and territorial integrity and pushing for increased regional stability.

Both parties underlined their support for the Palestinian cause.

The countries also agreed to celebrate the centenary of diplomatic relations next year with reciprocal visits and commemorative events, highlighting what both governments described as a strategic partnership that has expanded beyond security cooperation to include trade, energy, infrastructure, and regional connectivity.

World.title: Iraq PM publicly orders Transport Minister to sign Turkey corridor deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi publicly ordered his Transport Minister to sign a major agreement on the Development Road project at a joint ceremony with Turkish President Tayyip Erdoğan on Tuesday after an unexpected delay that temporarily interrupted the signing event.

The event occurred at a live broadcast ceremony in Ankara after the conclusion of discussions between Iraq and Turkey to strengthen cooperation in transportation, energy, and commerce.

Footage from the occasion shows Al-Zaidi interrogating Transport Minister Wahib al-Husseini about why the deal had not been signed before telling him to do it immediately.

Al-Zaidi then went to an interpreter, requesting that Erdogan be notified that he had instructed the Minister to sign.

The unexpected conversation temporarily overshadowed a tour meant to highlight progress on the Development Road project, a hallmark Iraqi program that would connect the Gulf’s Grand Faw Port to Turkey by a network of trains and roadways, establishing a significant commerce corridor between Asia and Europe.

Neither the Iraqi government nor Iraq’s Transport Ministry immediately stated the cause of the delay.

However, Iraqi politicians and media analysts said that al-Husseini originally delayed signing due to opposition from political groupings connected with the Iran-backed Badr Organization, led by Hadi al-Amiri, to whom the minister is affiliated.

According to the sources, opponents worried the corridor would reduce Iran’s position as a regional transit route.

The incident occurs at a crucial moment for Al-Zaidi, who has worked to establish Iraq as a regional transportation and logistics center while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

In recent weeks, the young Prime Minister has achieved a number of investment deals during travels to the United States, where American corporations have declared more than $60 billion in planned projects, and Iran, where Baghdad has inked transport and railway collaboration agreements.

He is also scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia later this week.

The Development Road initiative is fundamental to Iraq’s economic policy, with the goal of diversifying state income away from oil, increasing trade flows, and establishing Iraq as a major gateway linking the Gulf to Turkey and European markets.

The public dispute underscored Al-Zaidi’s political concerns as he strives to promote big economic changes while balancing opposing interests among Iraq’s strong political factions and armed organizations, some of whom have close links to Iran.

Analysts argue that managing those opposing interests remains one of his premiership’s most difficult challenges, as Baghdad seeks greater economic links with the United States, Turkey, and Gulf Arab governments while preserving relations with Tehran.

World.title: Saudi Arabia blames Iran-backed militias in Iraq for drone attack
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia claimed on Tuesday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed multiple drones targeting oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province, accusing Iran-backed militants operating from Iraq of carrying out the assault.

Major General Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi Defense Ministry, claimed the drones were intercepted many hours before reaching their objectives. He said that there were no immediate reports of damage or injuries.

Al-Maliki said that the drones were fired from Iraqi land by Iran-backed militias and that the strike was a terrorist act, adding that Saudi Arabia has the right to reply “at the appropriate time and place.”

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, and Iraqi officials had not independently verified Saudi Arabia’s claims.

The incident is the second occasion in recent days that Saudi Arabia has accused armed groups operating in Iraq of firing drones against the country.

Earlier, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi directed security agencies to investigate Saudi allegations that drones targeting the kingdom were launched from Iraqi territory, stating that Baghdad would prosecute anyone found responsible and emphasizing that Iraq would not allow its territory to be used to attack neighboring countries.

The latest accusation comes just days before Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia for talks with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, where the two sides are expected to discuss expanding investment, trade, and regional cooperation following the prime minister’s recent trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara.

The recurring instances highlight one of the most difficult difficulties for Al-Zaidi’s administration as it strives to develop relations with Gulf Arab governments while exerting state control over Iran-aligned armed organizations that have carried out assaults independent of the Iraqi government.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 526,000 bpd in May and June
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s average oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 526,470 barrels per day, compared to about 329,500 barrels per day in April, amid ongoing shipping and energy disruptions in the Gulf region.

The revenues generated from Iraqi oil exports saw an improvement over the last two months, supported by a relative increase in shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and the activation of alternative export routes.

Oil prices fluctuated, remaining high at around $100 per barrel during May before falling below that level in June.

The rising oil prices boosted Iraq’s export income in May and June 2026, when there were fears about supply constraints and increased Asian demand, notably from China and India.

Iraqi oil exports have been under growing strain since the beginning of March, following the suspension of loading operations at southern ports due to the US war against Iran, which had a direct impact on marine security in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO), Iraq’s total oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 32.11 million barrels, with a monthly average of over 16 million barrels.

The country’s oil exports reached 9.88 million barrels in April and around 18.6 million barrels in March.

Iraqi oil export earnings in May and June 2026 reached approximately $2.33 billion, averaging $1.16 billion per month, compared to $1.87 billion in April, $1.95 billion in March, and approximately $6.81 billion in February.

Experts believe that the current price levels of oil are likely to provide Baghdad with a better financial margin to mitigate some losses incurred from the significant decline in exports, even amidst ongoing security tensions in the region.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Turkey on an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Tuesday, for an official visit following an invitation from President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that his trip to Turkey will focus on investments, water, and development projects, as well as efforts to enhance stability in the region.

Turkish media highlighted the significance of the visit, as it is expected to broaden constructive collaboration between the two countries, particularly in the areas of water, energy, security, and economic cooperation, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

In addition to trade, security cooperation, and combating terrorism, al-Zaidi will discuss establishing a cooperative water management entity based on shared interests, as well as scientific collaboration and investment in advanced technology, to serve the interests of both Iraq and Turkey.

Al-Zaidi is scheduled to fly to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for an official visit, following his diplomatic trip to the Turkish capital, Ankara.

The trip is part of a larger regional diplomatic tour aiming to maintain regional balance and strengthen Iraq’s business connections.

The prime minister recently conducted high-level diplomatic visits to the United States on July 13 and Iran on July 23.

World.title: Ukraine rejects Iraqi official’s claims of Ukrainian cell operating in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday dismissed statements by Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi, who claimed that Iraqi authorities had arrested a Ukrainian-linked cell responsible for carrying out attacks inside the country.

In an official statement, the ministry said the allegations were “groundless” and noted that no evidence had been presented to support the claims. It also pointed out that Al-Aboudi himself acknowledged during a televised interview that investigations into the matter were still ongoing.

According to the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Iraqi authorities did not communicate any information or concerns through diplomatic channels before the allegations were made publicly.

The ministry said that if Iraqi officials possessed credible evidence, the issue should have been raised through official diplomatic mechanisms rather than announced during a television interview. Instead, Kyiv said it first learned of the accusations through media reports.

Furthermore, Ukraine described the public remarks by a senior Iraqi official as “unacceptable and irresponsible” in the absence of supporting evidence. The ministry stressed that such statements contradict the principles of mutual respect between friendly nations and risk undermining relations between Iraq and Ukraine.

At the same time, Kyiv reaffirmed that it considers Iraq an important partner in the Middle East and remains committed to strengthening political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation between the two countries.

The Foreign Ministry also argued that the allegations mirror Russian propaganda narratives aimed at damaging Ukraine’s international reputation and weakening its partnerships across the Middle East.

Additionally, the statement suggested that the incident could have resulted from external information influence or formed part of a coordinated information campaign intended to disrupt Iraqi-Ukrainian relations.

Ukraine called on Iraqi authorities to address what it described as unfounded allegations and to prevent state institutions from promoting misinformation that could serve the interests of third parties.

The Ukrainian response follows remarks made on Monday by National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi during an interview on Dijlah TV. Al-Aboudi said Iraqi intelligence had identified what he described as Ukrainian interference inside Iraq and claimed security forces had arrested several individuals who allegedly carried out attacks on Iraqi territory.

He further stated that those detained confessed during questioning to working on behalf of Ukraine. However, Al-Aboudi did not identify the facilities allegedly targeted or specify whether the alleged operations extended beyond Iraq’s borders.

He also acknowledged that investigations into attacks carried out inside Iraq remain complex and require further examination before responsibility can be definitively assigned.

World.title: Iraqi PM expands powers as political deadlock delays cabinet completion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A dispute over Iraq’s remaining vacant cabinet positions has expanded beyond the selection of ministers, with political factions now focusing on the growing authority of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, according to a report published by Al-Mada newspaper.

The debate follows the leak of an official document indicating that Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has reactivated and expanded the powers of the Commander-in-Chief Office, placing several key security institutions under its supervision while the Ministries of Interior and Defense remain without permanent ministers.

According to Al-Mada, several political sources believe the expanded office significantly increases the prime minister’s direct oversight of Iraq’s security apparatus.

The report says the office now oversees the Ministries of Interior and Defense, the Counter-Terrorism Service, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), border crossings, military industries, and other security-related institutions.

Consequently, some political figures have described the move as a “quiet coup” against Iraq’s post-2003 political framework, arguing that it centralizes authority within the prime minister’s office while reducing the practical influence of future ministers.

Meanwhile, Iraq’s cabinet remains incomplete, with only 14 ministries currently filled while nine ministerial portfolios remain vacant. According to the report, political negotiations have become increasingly complicated, as disagreements now extend beyond candidate names to broader questions of political influence and institutional control.

Sources cited by Al-Mada said the State of Law Coalition has proposed rotating senior security positions as part of efforts to break the deadlock, particularly regarding the Interior Ministry, which traditionally falls under the Shiite political share, while the Defense Ministry is typically allocated to Sunni representatives.

However, negotiations have yet to produce a breakthrough.

At the same time, Al-Mada reported that U.S. objections have become one of the main obstacles preventing completion of the cabinet. Political sources quoted in the report claim Washington opposes appointing individuals affiliated with armed factions to ministerial positions or senior executive offices.

The report says these objections have complicated negotiations among members of the Coordination Framework, with some factions insisting that if their nominees are rejected, similar restrictions should apply to other political parties. As a result, discussions over the remaining cabinet positions have largely stalled.

Political analysts interviewed by Al-Mada argue that the continued delay in appointing ministers has allowed Prime Minister Al-Zaidi greater flexibility in managing state institutions through acting officials and appointments within his office.

According to the report, some political parties fear that prolonging the vacancies could further strengthen the prime minister’s influence over Iraq’s security establishment, making future ministerial appointments less significant.

The report also notes that recent anti-corruption campaigns and shifting political alliances have altered the balance of power within the Coordination Framework, adding another layer of complexity to negotiations.

Supporters of the government, however, argue that the current arrangements are necessary to maintain continuity while negotiations continue.

Officials quoted by Al-Mada said acting appointments and the reactivation of the Commander-in-Chief Office ensure that security institutions continue functioning despite the absence of permanent ministers.

They also expressed confidence that political forces will eventually reach an agreement to complete the cabinet, stressing that Iraq faces significant challenges, including anti-corruption efforts, security reforms, weapons control, and economic pressures linked to oil exports.

Nevertheless, the report suggests that political parties continue to use the vacant ministries as leverage in negotiations with the prime minister, making the timeline for completing the government uncertain.

World.title: US drone shot down in western Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An unknown drone, first claimed by Iranian official media IRIB as a US surveillance one, crashed within a residential complex near the Haditha Dam in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

Iraqi police and security agencies later indicated that the drone’s origin remains unknown, according to Al-Jazeera.

The debris was discovered blazing in a residential compound near the Haditha Dam in Anbar.

Local police stated that there were no recorded injuries or civilian deaths as a result of the collision.

Iranian state media swiftly released images of the smoking debris, claiming it was a US drone shot down amid broader regional activity.

The incident took place during a night of broad military conflict in Iraq, which included many drone attacks and defensive responses.

At least four Iranian drones attacked targets northeast of the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil, sparking a huge defensive reaction, including over ten US jets and drones sent to inspect the skies.

Air defense systems were activated at Anbar’s Ain al-Asad Air Base in response to a drone strike.

Explosions, alleged suicide drones, and radar interruptions were also reported at Camp Taji, Balad Air Base, and Imam Ali Base in southern Iraq.

The US military has not publicly verified the loss of any aircraft in Anbar. Investigations into the model and operator of the crashed drone are still underway.

World.title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
World.content:
File photo: July 20 NEET protest march

âPolice, RAF attacked with stones, iron railsâ

NEW DELHI: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun, a CRPF post-event analysis has said.CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob. Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.When contacted, CRPF DG G P Singh said the matter was "sub judice" and any findings or view of the force on RAF action would be placed before Supreme Court. RAF sources said the use of force on July 20 was authorised by Delhi Police, in line with the SOPs and the law.Sources claimed the mob had some motivated elements attacking personnel of Delhi Police and RAF with stones and, in some cases, even iron rails.As per BNSS, an executive magistrate may order use of civil force to disperse an unlawful assembly after carefully assessing the situation.In Delhi, this magisterial authority is vested with the Delhi Police commissioner, and delegated to junior commissioners till the level of the assistant commissioner of police. âRAF deployed at protest sites uses anti-riot gear only with authorisation; which in this case came from the DCP/ACP in charge of the protest site. Such authorisation is in writing and as per a format used at all sites of unlawful assembly; no order is given verbally,â said an officer.CRPF sources said pump action guns are an approved, ânon-lethalâ measure to control unlawful assemblies. âTheir use, with the force gradient being followed and under authorisation by the competent officer, is as per the SOP,â said an officer.J&K high court had, in its 2016 ruling on a PIL challenging pellet use, said: âSo long as there is violence by unruly mobs, use of force is inevitable. What kind of force has to be used at the relevant point of time or in a given situation has to be decided by the persons in charge of the place where the attack is happening. This court in writ jurisdiction, without any finding rendered by the competent forum/authority cannot decide whether the use of force in a particular incident is excessive or not. âSupreme Court later dismissed the special leave petition against this order, stating, âThe use of pellet guns, if at all done by any agency, has not only not been barred, but validated through these orders.â

World.title: India is second-largest sailor supplier in world
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With a 12.2% share of global seafaring workforce, India has become the world's second-largest supplier of sailors, according to BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026.

The Philippines continues to be the largest supplier of seafarers globally.

The report published every five years is widely regarded by the global maritime industry as the most authoritative assessment of seafarer supply and demand. As per the report, share of Indian sailors has doubled in the past five years.

"BIMCO-ICS report is the most credible and every maritime nation follows this. India's strength is particularly evident in the officer cadre. We supply over 1.4 lakh officers, accounting for 13.4% of the world's officer workforce, while 1.7 lakh ratings represent 11.29% of the global ratings serving aboard merchant vessels," said an official.

World.title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
World.content:
SG Mehta said the government will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to the SC in a sealed cover

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday accepted the request of the father of the pilot, who died in the Ahmedabad air crash last June, for not making public the final inquiry report, expected in Oct, and the Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that govt respects the sentiments of the pilot's father and will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to Supreme Court in a sealed cover. The SG, however, brushed aside objections to the ongoing inquiry into the crash of Air India's London flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground.Appearing for the NGO, advocate Prashant Bhushan attempted to punch holes in the inquiry, terming it to be biased because of absence of independent members in the probe team and said it did not follow the standard operating procedure for such inquiries. The solicitor general said the inquiry is being conducted following prescribed process scrupulously.Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on July 14 had responded to the petition filed by the deceased pilot's father Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, and said, "In view of the nature, scale and complexity of the present accident, the AAIB has carefully assessed the timeline for completion of the investigation.In all probability, the investigation activities, subject to resolution of the pending external dependencies, are anticipated to be completed within six weeks. ""Thereafter, the draft final report, following completion of the analysis phase, is expected to be ready approximately in Oct 2026," it had said. "As per the treaty mandate, upon preparation of draft final report, the same has to be mandatorily shared with the Accredited Representatives of the State of Design and Manufacture, for comments, as required under the relevant rules of International Civil Aviation Organisation , which in the present case - the National Transportation Safety Board, USA. "

World.title: 'Every possible measure must be taken': Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says no Indian seafarer should be caught in crossfire
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid escalating geopolitical tensions affecting key global shipping routes and posing risks to Indian sailors, shipping minister

Tuesday directed officials to ensure âno Indian seafarer finds himself caught in the crossfire of geopolitical conflictâ.

Safety of Indian mariners remains govtâs top priority, he said while chairing a high-level review meeting on the safety and welfare of Indian seafarers serving aboard merchant vessels in conflict-sensitive regions. The meeting was attended by officials from different departments and heads of Indian missions in Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Russia and Ukraine.

âNo Indian seafarer should find himself caught in the crossfire of geopolitical conflict.

Every possible measure must be taken to safeguard our seafarers, support their families and ensure timely assistance wherever required,â the minister said.

Meanwhile, on X, Forward Seamenâs Union of India (FSUI) claimed that AMIR1, currently at Ukrainian port Chornomorsk with 15 crew on board, including 13 Indian seafarers, was trapped in a âterrible and life-threatening situationâ.

It said, âRepeated drone and missile attacks are being attempted in the immediate vicinity of the vessel.





The crew is living under constant fear of a direct hit at any moment,â while appealing to authorities, shipowners, flag state, and govt to immediately secure their safety and arrange prompt repatriation.

During the meeting, officials reviewed the prevailing security situation, maritime developments and the preparedness of Indian diplomatic missions.

DG Shipping informed the minister that its 24x7 Seafarer Grievance and Assistance Cell remains fully operational.

It added that to strengthen preparedness, the maritime regulator has asked Recruitment and Placement Service Licensees (RPSLs) to conduct structured pre-departure orientation programmes to familiarise seafarers with operational conditions, security protocols and evolving geopolitical risks in deployment areas.

Recognising the psychological stress of prolonged deployment in volatile regions, Sonowal also directed officials to integrate mental health support into the seafarer welfare framework, including counselling services for seafarers and their families and greater transparency on operational risks before deployment.

World.title: 'I regret it': Mehbooba Mufti claims Jantar Mantar remark a slip of tongue, apologises
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Under fire for her Jantar Mantar remark that appeared to justify the use of force in Kashmir on grounds of âmilitancyâ, PDP president

Tuesday apologised, but claimed it was a slip of tongue and accused governing NC and chief minister

of deliberately misinterpreting her comment.

âIf my words have hurt or upset my people, who consider me one of their own and often hold me accountable even over small matters, then I sincerely apologise,â Mehbooba said. âIf they have been hurt by my statement, I regret it.â

Explaining the controversial remark, she said: âOne clip from my interaction, in which I used the word âbanta haiâ (understandable) while referring to militancy, went viral. I said that in haste.

The remark was interpreted differently.â

While talking to reporters at Jantar Mantar on July 23 during the CJP protest, Mehbooba is heard saying in a widely circulated video: âWe have seen this (use of force against protesters) for the first time in Delhi. We have witnessed it in Kashmir for many years. Magar wahan militancy hai, uska ek banta hai (But militancy exists there, so it is understandable).â

With Omar lapping up the remark and accusing her of supporting the repression of Kashmiris, the former J&K chief minister clarified she meant to say âbahanaâ (excuse) banta hai, but in a slip of tongue, said âbanta haiâ.





âThe video circulating is genuine, but the meaning being attributed to my words is not,â she said.

NC, however, rejected her apology and clarification. âThe only appropriate response is a clear and unconditional apology to every Kashmiri who was hurt, especially the victims of pellet injuries,â party spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq said.

âAlso, apologise for your alliance with BJP and for bringing them to power in Jammu & Kashmir. Everything else said today was simply an attempt to divert attention from your original remarks,â he added.

World.title: ‘It hurts to remember’: Blind since 14, J&K pellet survivor searches for tomorrow
World.content:
SEDOW(SHOPIAN): Behind a mesh screen, Insha Mushtaq sits in a mustard headscarf, offering a faint smile. She cannot see the camera or the daylight filtering through her window. She only senses.

Ten years after pellets took her eyes during J&Kâs 2016 unrest, she still carries scars that have become public property, resurfacing every time India debates crowd control.

She wishes they wouldnât. âI donât want to remember. It doesnât help and it hurts,â said the 24-year-old, seated inside her home in Sedow village of Shopian, about 75km south of Srinagar.

Yet memory has a stubborn half-life. Images of 14-year-old Insha, her face wrapped in bandages after being struck by pellets during protests following Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Waniâs killing, travelled across TV screens and social media in 2016.

They turned her into perhaps J&Kâs most recognisable face of pellet gun wounds. Every fresh political quarrel over use of force drags those photographs back into public view.

Insha Mushtaq has been blind since 14

Recent protests over NEET irregularities in New Delhi have done exactly that.

For Insha, the debate translates into reopening wounds she has spent years trying to close. âI donât know whether I should talk or not. I want to do a job after completing my education,â she said, her father Mushtaq Ahmad Lone and mother Afroza Akhtar sitting quietly beside her.





She has not abandoned her future. Blindness altered her life, not her ambition. She is completing a bachelorâs degree in arts and hopes to find a govt job under disability quota. Speaking publicly, she fears, could jeopardise that dream.

âI donât know what happened in Delhi but I know many lives were destroyed by pellet guns in Kashmir,â she said. Then her face brightened. âI am blind but we can operate phones.â

Pellet guns entered J&Kâs security arsenal around 2010 as a supposedly non-lethal alternative to bullets.

They left behind hundreds of eye wounds, partial blindness and permanent loss of vision. Years dulled national attention, but memories never disappeared. Protests in New Delhi breathed fresh life into an old controversy.

Political sparring has followed. Governing National Conference has accused opposition Peoples Democratic Party of condemning pellet guns in New Delhi while defending their use in J&K. PDP, in turn, has blamed CM Omar Abdullah for introducing pellet guns during his earlier tenure to tackle protests after about 110 demonstrators were killed in security action during 2009-10.

According to BJP, use of bullets and pellets ceased after Article 370âs abrogation in 2019 because protests largely ended.

Former J&K DGP SP Vaid, who headed police during 2016 unrest, said pellet guns were first used during 2009-10 protests and again in 2016. âAll those 110 people killed in 2010 died due to bullets not pellets. Pellet gun should be used only as a last resort, from a proper distance and aimed below the waist,â Vaid said.

Describing them as 12-bore pump-action guns, he said: âIâm not saying pellet guns are good. I am saying they are a better last-resort option than direct firing with live ammunition. If the choice is between bullets and pellet guns, pellet guns can save lives.â

Politics feels distant inside Inshaâs two-storey home. She now climbs stairs unaided. Certificates marking completion of classes 11 and 12 line her room. But July 12, 2016 remains etched with painful clarity.

Clashes had broken out outside her home. Tear gas shells landed nearby. Curious, she walked to a window overlooking the village road. The instant she opened it, a volley of pellets shattered glass and ripped into her face. âMy forehead felt like it was burning from inside,â she said.

She was taken first to Shopian district hospital before doctors referred her to Shri Maharaja Hari Singh Hospital in Srinagar. She slipped into a coma for 4 days.

Her photographs quickly became emblematic of 2016 unrest, prompting intervention by then PDP-BJP govt. Then CM Mehbooba Mufti promised assistance â gave Inshaâs father a job. After spending nearly a month at SMHS Hospital, Insha was shifted to AIIMS New Delhi, where she remained for almost 2 months.

On Sept 13, 2016, she was moved to Aditya Jyot Eye Hospital in Mumbai, where ophthalmologist Dr S Natarajan treated her for nearly 24 days.

Natarajan, then hospital director and president of Ocular Trauma Society of India, operated on hundreds of pellet survivors during repeated visits to J&K that year.

Doctors eventually told her family she had no perception of light. Blindness would be lifelong.

An intervention proved transformative. âNadir

helped me continue my education. He kept insisting that I should study. Had he not been there, I would have been finished,â Insha said.

Ali, chairperson of J&K Centre for Peace and Justice Foundation, first met her in late 2017. âShe was not born blind. She was angry, very angry and undergoing surgeries regularly for removal of pellets,â he said.

Ali admitted her to special education department at Delhi Public School in Srinagar, where she spent nearly 2 years learning Braille, mobility skills and computer applications. âWhen I visited her home, I saw people had given her certificates but no one seemed to be thinking about how she would build a future,â he said.

âShe wanted to study and I wanted to help her. She had to learn how to walk independently, use a computer and adapt to a completely new way of life.

â

Today, Insha studies political science, English, education and sociology through Ignou. Graduation is within reach. âThis is her final yearâ¦ Our aim is to make her financially independent,â Ali said.

Ali has another appeal, one directed at journalists: âOnce you tell them to recount their past, they again slip into trauma. Let them heal.â For Insha, that may be hardest of all. The country remembers a photograph. She lives its aftermath.

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Bus with Amarnath pilgrims slips into gorge, 39 hurt
World.content:
SRINAGAR: At least 39 Amarnath pilgrims, including 21 from Madhya Pradesh and 19 Rajasthan natives, were injured after their bus skidded off the road in Ganiwan in J&Kâs Ganderbal district and slipped into a 50-foot-deep gorge on Tuesday morning.

The fall was broken midway at around 25 feet by a house in a mountain hamlet below the road, preventing the vehicle from sliding further down the slope and averting a major tragedy, locals said.

The devotees were heading back after visiting the holy cave shrine. The vehicle was moving from Baltal towards Srinagar when the accident occurred around 7 am near Ranga Morh, prompting a multi-agency rescue operation. Residents said the house belonged to Din Mohammad, who was away grazing sheep with his family at the time.

J&K Police, CRPF, ITBP, health department and civil defence personnel rushed to the spot and launched a coordinated rescue operation, with assistance from locals. The injured were moved to SKIMS in Soura, Srinagar.

J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited SKIMS, where doctors briefed him about the health condition of those injured. In an X post, Sinha said he instructed officials to ensure the best possible treatment for the hospitalised pilgrims and arrangements for their safe return upon recovery.





Health minister Sakeena Itoo also visited SKIMS and interacted with the injured pilgrims, assuring them of full govt support. She directed hospital authorities to monitor each patientâs condition and ensure round-the-clock availability of specialist doctors and essential healthcare services.

This year's Amarnath Yatra began on July 3. The 57-day annual pilgrimage will conclude on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan. As of July 26, more than 4,14,000 pilgrims had completed the annual pilgrimage and offered prayers at the holy cave shrine.

World.title: CBI files chargesheet against 13 accused in NEET-UG paper leak case; hearing tomorrow
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Tuesday filed a chargesheet against 13 accused in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak case before the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi.

The chargesheet, filed by the Economic Offences Wing of the CBI, will be placed before the special fast-track court constituted to hear paper leak cases on Wednesday.

According to the agency, the case has been registered under Sections 315(5), 318(4), 61(2), 238 and 303(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, along with Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(a) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and Sections 3, 4, 5, 10 and 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

As per the information shared by ANI, the accused named in the chargesheet are Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh Biwal, Vikas Biwal, Subham Khairnar, Dhananjay Lokhande, Prahalad Kulkarni, Tejas Harshad Kumar, Dr Manoj Shirure, Shivraj Raghunath Motegaonkar, Manisha Waghmare, Manisha Mandhare, and Manisha Sanjay Hawaldar.

All 13 accused are currently in judicial custody.

The alleged leak of the NEET-UG examination paper triggered nationwide outrage and led to multiple investigations into irregularities in the conduct of the medical entrance examination.





Dharmendra Pradhan also resigned on July 25 as Union education minister, following which the Cockroach Janta Party withdrew its 36-day agitation that had mobilised lakhs of people over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and the NEET paper leak.

World.title: Unwise to link women’s quota with delimitation: K.T. Rama Rao
World.content:
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leader K.T. Rama Rao (KTR), said that the protests by students over the leak of the NEET exam paper was “unique” and an “inflexion” point in Indian polity and that the Delimitation Bill, if it is tabled in Parliament, should ensure that the southern States maintain their level of representation in the Lok Sabha.

Speaking to The Hindu during his visit to Delhi, Mr. Rao said that the protests were not just about paper leaks but seemed to be channelling a number of frustrations among the people that needed a trigger point. While anti-incumbency had built up, he said, he conceded that the BJP still had time to recover, but that the lessons for the Opposition were just as dire.

“What you effectively saw was the manifestation of a series of events and not just one isolated incident that resulted in this. They (the BJP) still have time to make amends and maybe win the youngsters back. Also the situation clearly shows that it was not the principle Opposition nor the Opposition block as such, that could inspire confidence, and it had to be a student led, kind of leaderless, rudderless kind of a moment, which just emanated like the Arab Spring had (in 2011). Therefore, it’s unique and it certainly is an inflection point in Indian politics. If you ask me, Prime Minister Modi and his government has never looked as vulnerable as they did in the last 15 days,” he said.

On delimitation Mr. Rao said that it was “unwise” to intertwine women reservation and delimitation the way the government had done in April in the special session to consider the two Bills.

“Women’s reservation can be implemented without linking it or without intertwining it with delimitation. So the fundamental point of Government of India trying to fire the delimitation gun, you know, using a women reservation as a shoulder to lean on is wrong, whereas the Women’s Reservation Act has already been passed by Parliament,” he said. “Government of India needs to realise that they’re sitting on a powder keg. If they mess with the current ratio, where the southern States as a block have 24% representation in Parliament, then most certainly there will be a serious protest erupting in the south,” he said.

He suggested his own formula for doing so. “Why is delimitation done in the first place? Because you want increased participation, representative democracy, more decentralisation, etc. So the one way to do it, is basically increase the number of MLA seats. If they can go ahead and increase the number of MLA seats across the country, there’s 4000 plus now. That can be enhanced to 6000. Nobody has a problem. Because then it’s within the geographical confines of one State and when it comes to Parliament, you’re not disturbing the status quo. The second formula could be one where you actually sit across a table, come to the consensus on how this 24% of South can be maintained as is, so that there is parity and balance,” he said.

“There should not be a penalty for good implementation of population policies, you can’t have a noose around our neck, say that this is good for you (southern States), and stifle our voice,” he said.

World.title: Paper leak Bill a milestone, says govt; Opposition calls it ‘cosmetic exercise’
World.content:
Treasury and Opposition benches sparred in the Lok Sabha on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) as the House took up the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, with the Opposition describing it as an “admission of failure”.

Also read | Bill proposing harsher punishment for paper leaks taken up for discussion; milestone legislation, says government

Initiating the debate for the Opposition, Congress deputy leader Gaurav Gogoi questioned why the government was amending a law it had hailed as “historic” just two years ago.

“If that law was so effective, why has the government been forced to bring such major amendments within two years?” Mr. Gogoi asked, calling the Bill a “cosmetic exercise” that reflected the failure of the 2024 law enacted after the earlier NEET-UG controversy.

He argued that the latest paper leak had exposed the government’s inability to protect the integrity of public examinations and said harsher punishments alone would not end the menace without structural reforms in the education system.

Referring to the nationwide student protests, Mr. Gogoi condemned the use of pellet guns and electric batons, saying students had taken to the streets out of “deep pain and anxiety” over their future.

The Congress leader also questioned the fate of recommendations by the 2024 committee headed by former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan and sought details of the 47 officials the government claimed to have removed or transferred from the National Testing Agency (NTA).

“Who are these 47 people, when the sanctioned strength of the NTA is 34?” Mr. Gogoi asked. He also questioned why the government had so much faith in the NTA chairman. “Is it because he is associated with a particular Sangh?” he asked.

The Congress leader also alleged that 44 of the 45 accused in the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak case had secured bail.

Mr. Gogoi and several other MPs objected to BJP MP Dharmendra Pradhan being given a “grand welcome” by his party colleagues in Parliament even after he had to resign as the Union Education Minister. “It is as if he had won a war with Pakistan,” Mr. Gogoi said.

Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Dimple Yadav lashed out at the government for the police action against protesting students. “The government could pressurise some of the MPs sitting here to try and pass the Delimitation Bill, but it could not put pressure on students,” she said, while reading out the names of the students who allegedly died by suicide over the NEET paper leak.

BJP counters

Responding to the Opposition, BJP MP Anurag Thakur hit out at Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi for sitting on a dharna outside the Prime Minister’s residence, saying Mr. Gandhi did so because students did not ask him to lead the protests.

Mr. Thakur also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi continues to be popular among the country’s youth, adding his Instagram video on the issue had garnered over 400 million views.

Defending the Bill, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accused the Opposition of “selective outrage”, contending that paper leaks had also occurred under the UPA government’s tenure. Calling the amendment “transformative”, she said it would strengthen the legal framework through faster prosecution, stricter punishment and measures to tackle organised examination mafias.

Shiv Sena MP Shrikanth Shinde accused the Opposition of politicising the issue while the Modi government is taking decisive steps to tackle examination paper leaks.

World.title: India’s Gen Z wants Pakistan to end terror activities: govt
World.content:
India on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) reiterated that Pakistan continues to promote cross-border terrorism as a state policy, with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) saying Pakistan’s Gen Z should "take note" that people of India, including the Indian Gen Z, are aware of Islamabad’s support for terrorism against India.

“As we are all aware, Pakistan has been sponsoring cross-border terrorism against India for decades. The people of India, including Gen Z, have been demanding that the Pakistani state-sponsored cross-border terrorism must come to an end. We hope their counterparts are taking due note,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, regarding the online support extended by the Pakistani social media handlers to the Cockroach Janta Party’s recent protest at Jantar Mantar. Mr. Jaiswal was speaking at the bi-weekly media briefing.

The protest at Jantar Mantar attracted solidarity and commentary from a section of Pakistani social media users. However, officials here pointed out that online bonhomie is unlikely to influence the currently frozen state of India-Pakistan relations.

They argued that India has put the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance after the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and said that bilateral ties remain frozen because of Pakistan’s support for cross-border terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir.

Referring to Pakistan’s attempts to project itself as the inheritor of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, Mr. Jaiswal said that as a supporter of terrorism, Pakistan cannot lay any claim to a “pluralistic cultural legacy” like the Indus Valley Civilisation.

“Their abysmal track record on the protection of minorities and their cultural rights makes such desperate attempts look even more phoney,” said Mr. Jaiswal while responding to a question.

World.title: Rajnath Singh unveils Coast Guard reforms to boost gender equality
World.content:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) unveiled two major policy reforms for the Indian Coast Guard (ICG), introducing a gender-neutral framework for the induction and career progression of officers and simplifying the process of granting ex gratia compensation to the families of personnel reported missing at sea while on duty.

The reforms were announced at an event held at Kartavya Bhavan-2 in New Delhi, attended by Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, Director General, Indian Coast Guard, Paramesh Sivamani and other senior officials.

The Ministry of Defence described the measures as forward-looking reforms. Mr Singh said they would strengthen the force's morale and operational effectiveness as it prepares to celebrate its Swarnim Jayanti (Golden Jubilee) in 2027. He reiterated the government’s commitment to building a modern, capable and future-ready Coast Guard under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The first policy introduces a comprehensive gender-neutral framework for officer induction. It allows women to be inducted through both Short Service Appointment (SSA) and Permanent Appointment (PA) streams on par with their male counterparts, while opening the SSA entry route for male candidates as well.

Equal opportunities

The policy also ensures equal opportunities for career progression from the initial training stage. Existing women officers holding Permanent Appointments will be eligible for promotion to higher ranks subject to prescribed conditions, while serving women officers under the SSA scheme will have the option to convert to Permanent Appointment after meeting the stipulated eligibility criteria.

The Defence Ministry said the reform reflected the government’s commitment to promoting Nari Shakti and ensuring equal opportunities within India’s maritime security framework.

The second reform aims to provide timely financial relief to the next of kin of Coast Guard personnel who go missing at sea while performing their duties. Under the new policy, the competent authority will be empowered to declare such personnel as “presumed dead” solely for the purpose of processing ex-gratia compensation and terminal benefits.

The Ministry said the revised procedure would significantly reduce administrative delays, enabling bereaved families to receive financial assistance and service benefits without prolonged waiting periods during times of distress.

World.title: NEET violence: Supreme Court debates yet to detail if Delhi Police kept Home Ministry in the loop
World.content:
Little has been said in the Supreme Court so far about instructions or consultations between the Delhi Police and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) as violence unfolded in NEET-UG protests in the national capital on July 20.

The Supreme Court judgment of February 2012 in the Ramlila Maidan Incident versus Home Secretary refers to the then Delhi Police Commissioner’s affidavit that “as a matter of practice, Delhi Police keep the Ministry of Home Affairs duly informed in such matters”.

The judgment said the affidavit had reasoned that the MHA “for obvious reasons, is concerned about the preservation of law and order in the capital and carefully monitors all situations dealing with public order and tranquility”.

The court had recorded from the affidavit that it was “also clear that he [Police Commissioner] was continuously in touch with the senior functionaries of the Ministry of Home Affairs”, and had kept them clued in on the decisions taken by senior police officers on the ground. Under Article 239AA of the Constitution, the MHA has control over the Delhi Police.

The stand of the political executive would be a crucial part of the Supreme Court hearings into the NEET-UG protests, especially with one of the petitions claiming that the police action on July 20 against students protesting peacefully was “no less than the atrocities of the Jallianwala Bagh”. Independently, outside the court room, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha has reportedly asked in a letter whether the Home Minister had authorised the use of “lethal force”.

The Supreme Court, over the decades, has shown a keen awareness and concern about political influence over the police.

Twenty years ago, a Supreme Court judgment in the Prakash Singh case had cautioned against the overwhelming influence the political executive could wield over the police. The 2006 judgment had been based on a petition arguing the point that reducing the police to a mere tool in the hands of political masters would result in serious violations of the rights of the people.

The 2006 judgment had referred to a research paper ‘Political and Administrative Manipulation of the Police’ published in 1979 by Bureau of Police Research and Development, warning that “excessive control of the political executive and its principal advisers over the police has the inherent danger of making the police a tool for subverting the process of law, promoting the growth of authoritarianism, and shaking the very foundations of democracy”. One of the issues mentioned in the judgment was police conduct in large-scale civil unrest.

The Prakash Singh case judgment had elaborated that political influence over the police was a reality by quoting from an April 3 1997 letter of the then Home Minister to State governments. The letter had underscored that many of the deficiencies in the functioning of the police had arisen largely due to an overdose of unhealthy and petty political interference.

The Union Home Minister, the judgment said, had exhorted the “great national importance to insulate the police from the growing tendency of partisan or political interference in the discharge of its lawful functions of prevention and control of crime including investigation of cases and maintenance of public order”.

The court has consistently held that respect for the rights of individuals was the “true bastion of democracy”. The liability was on the state to repair the damage done by its officers to their rights.

World.title: Maharashtra government decides to withdraw FIRs against protesters; police continue investigation
World.content:
The Maharashtra government has announced the withdrawal of First Information Reports (FIRs) registered against students and youth involved in recent protests. However, legal procedures, including the recording of statements and issuance of notices, continue as the investigation remains active. On July 28, some protesters received FIR notices via WhatsApp, leading to fresh allegations from student organisations.

A day after the State government directed the Home Department to withdraw cases against protesters, the Mumbai Police have stated that investigation procedures will continue until a formal order to halt the process is received. This development has created confusion among the student community and activists.

The decision to withdraw the cases came after a joint delegation of the All India Students’ Federation (AISF) met the Director General of Police and the Commissioner of Police. The delegations demanded an end to police harassment and the withdrawal of all FIRs lodged against peaceful demonstrators.

While the government has agreed to the demand, senior police officials have clarified that a probe cannot be stopped midway. According to the legal framework, the process of withdrawing FIRs related to political or social movements begins only after a charge sheet is filed. “Until the charge sheet is submitted, recording statements of accused and witnesses, conducting panchnamas, and other legal formalities are necessary. The cases then go to a scrutiny committee which recommends withdrawal,” an official said.

AISF Mumbai President Aamir Kazi stated that despite the announcement, students and youth are still receiving calls and notices, creating fear and confusion. He added that the Director General of Police has suggested that AISF submit a representation to the Mumbai Police Commissioner, urging them not to send new notices to protesters and to stop calling them to police stations.

On July 28, starting from 9:30 a.m., several students and youth who participated in the protests received FIR notices on WhatsApp, according to the Harsha Disha student organisation. In a statement, Harsha Disha said:

“Once again, the promises made by the Modi government have proven to be nothing more than false hopes. Since 9:30 a.m., students and youth who participated in the protests have been receiving FIR notices on WhatsApp. This is a clear tactic by the Mumbai Police and the BJP government to intimidate and spread fear among the youth, discouraging them from raising further questions or participating in future protests. Our appeal is that the student-youth movement must not rest until all FIRs filed against protesting students are withdrawn and all police officers who incited violence are held legally accountable for their actions. The CJP must stand by its initial demands and revive the protests until every FIR against the protesting students is withdrawn.” – Harsha Disha student organisations, who got FIR on WhatsApp on July 28.

The current government resolution on withdrawal of cases is valid until July 31. Officials noted that many investigations are ongoing and charge sheets may not be filed before that date, making an extension likely. “The sooner charge sheets are filed, the sooner the process of withdrawal under the government resolution can begin,” an officer added.

The AISF has welcomed the government’s decision but maintained that the struggle continues until every notice and legal proceeding against peaceful protesters is withdrawn. The federation has reiterated its demand for an immediate halt to police visits to the homes of protesters and an end to all forms of harassment.

World.title: Release all minors held over student protests: Supreme Court
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) indicated that it would consider constituting a high-powered investigation team to conduct a “thorough, fair and independent” inquiry into allegations of police excesses during the recent student protests in Delhi and several States. While permitting the State authorities to proceed with the investigation of the FIRs registered in relation to the protests, the court ordered the immediate release of all minors arrested in connection with the demonstrations and restrained the police from taking coercive action against “protesting students” unless they had criminal antecedents.

The interim order permitting the authorities to proceed with the investigation of the existing FIRs raised concerns among the protesters on Tuesday, with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which spearheaded the demonstrations, contending that the direction was contrary to the Centre’s assurance that no punitive action would be taken against protesters. Saurav Das, the CJP’s spokesperson, said in a post on X that the order “raises extremely serious concerns” and is in “direct contradiction” to the Centre’s assurance to the “youth of this nation”.

While underlining that the Constitution guarantees the right to peaceful protest, a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant observed that an independent probe was necessary to examine the allegations of police violence through a “scientific” and “evidence-based” inquiry.

“The allegations made by the petitioners, prima facie, establish a compelling case for an independent and impartial investigation into the incidents of violence”, the Bench observed, adding that the proposed probe would also examine complaints by the families of police personnel who were allegedly injured during the protests.

The interim directions came while the top court was hearing a batch of petitions alleging the use of disproportionate force by the police against protesters during demonstrations over the NEET examination paper leak, including the July 20 Parliament march in Delhi and subsequent protests in several States. The Hindu had earlier reported that at least four persons were struck by pellets during the Parliament march and that the Rapid Action Force (RAF) fired two rounds from an anti-riot gun on the directions of a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)-rank officer.

The Bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, issued notices to the Union government, the Delhi government and the Chief Secretaries of Maharashtra, Bihar, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Kerala, directing them to place their responses on record. It indicated that it would decide whether to order an independent probe after considering the responses filed by the authorities.

Continue probe, release detained minors

Taking note of petitions alleging that student protesters had been illegally arrested and detained by the police, the top court directed the authorities to forthwith release all minors detained in connection with the demonstrations. It clarified that, where required, they may be released on the “execution of a simple bond by themselves or their family members”, if such a requirement was insisted upon for furnishing surety.

While permitting the police to continue investigating the FIRs registered in relation to the protests, it restrained the authorities from taking any coercive action against students unless they had criminal antecedents.

“The NCT of Delhi and other States may proceed with the investigation of the FIRs registered; however, no coercive measures shall be taken against the protesting students. Such protection, nonetheless, shall not be extended to the persons with criminal antecedents,” the Bench ordered.

As an interim measure, the Bench directed the police authorities to preserve all CCTV footage, drone recordings, body-worn camera footage, wireless communication records and PCR call records relating to the protests. It also ordered that while the police may preserve the digital data of protesters for the purposes of the investigation, they shall not disclose any personal information in the public domain.

“The police authorities shall ensure that the personal information and digital data of the protestors, collected during the students’ protests, are preserved and are not disclosed to the public domain for the time being. The respondent(s) may not publish any public data/details of the protestors, especially students”, the Bench said.

‘Fix responsibility’

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for petitioner Shailendra Mani Tripathi, referred to videographic evidence allegedly showing the use of pellet guns and electric batons against protesters and urged the court to fix accountability. He also questioned the absence of any prohibitory orders in the Jantar Mantar area, the lack of name tags on police personnel and the deployment of officers in plain clothes for crowd-control duties.

“We have named individual police personnel, with video, who are responsible for this action... These people behaved with a licence... We want responsibility placed above the ladder. Police think they can get away with this,” he said.

Echoing these concerns, senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for one of the petitioners, placed on record photographs allegedly depicting the use of pellet guns and police personnel in plain clothes using force against protesters. “There are reports of electric shock weapons being used on protesters. The RAF has admitted the use of projectile-action guns (PAGs) against unarmed protesters. We have set out the details and placed credible media reports on record,” he submitted.

Appearing for a law student who was allegedly illegally detained by the Bihar police, senior advocate Shadan Farasat submitted that nearly 150 individuals, most of them minors, continued to remain in custody.

Acknowledging the concerns raised by the petitioners, the Chief Justice observed that an independent probe would look into the allegations and ensure that the law dealt with any excesses or atrocities found to have been committed by police personnel.

“Whosoever has committed excess, committed atrocities on innocent people, the law will take care of them. For that, there needs to be a completely independent and fair investigation…Probe is meaningless if no responsibility is fixed,” he said.

Notably, the court also indicated that it may revisit its earlier decisions governing police responses to public demonstrations, observing that a uniform protocol was required to regulate police conduct during such protests. It said the principles evolved in earlier decisions, including those arising from the 2011 Ramlila Maidan incident, may require reconsideration with the efflux of time.
